patch.name: Machine room hum (loop)
patch.description: The plant room in the basement of an office block: a transformer humming at 100 Hz with its buzzing odd partials, a big extraction fan turning at 1500 rpm behind a grille, air pushing through the ducts, and every second or two a contactor clacking somewhere in a cabinet. Concrete walls, so everything is a little boxy. A 4 s loop: the hum (50 Hz and its multiples) and the fan (25 turns a second) both fit a whole number of times, and the seam is crossfaded over 300 ms.

tracks.note: The transformer: mains hum at 100 Hz with strong 200, 300 and 400 Hz partials (so it is audible on small speakers) and a slow beat between its cores.
The extraction fan: an electric motor at 1500 rpm with seven blades, a soft drone and blade-passing flutter.
Air in the sheet-metal ducts: steady noise ringing faintly in a long tube. The "room tone" between the tones.
Contactors in the switch cabinets: a hard plastic-and-metal clack now and then. They break up the drone and say "this place is running".

controls.label: Hum
controls.hint: A faint electrical presence to a transformer you feel in your teeth.

controls.label: Ventilation
controls.hint: Still air to a roaring extraction system.

controls.label: Activity
controls.hint: A plant ticking over at night to switchgear clacking constantly.

controls.label: Room
controls.hint: A small cupboard of a room to a long concrete hall.

patch.name: Spaceship engine room (loop)
patch.description: The engine room of an old long-haul freighter under way: the reactor core throbs once every two seconds, a deep unstable tone that never quite repeats, the plasma conduits sing a slow swirling chord above it, coolant hisses through the pipes, and a status panel pings to itself in the corner. Steel walls, a tank of a room. An 8 s stereo loop; the throb and the swirl are tied to the loop length (0.5 and 0.125 Hz) and the seam is crossfaded over 1 s.

tracks.note: The reactor: a Lorenz attractor as a low tone that wanders between two states, swelling every 2 s. Alive and slightly worrying.
The plasma conduits: a detuned FM chord with a slow phaser sweep, the "technology" above the rumble.
Coolant and air handling: a band of hiss that drifts, so the room has air in it.
A status panel: sparse, soft, high pings at slightly different pitches. Scale and a sign of life.

controls.label: Power
controls.hint: Drifting on standby to engines at full burn: higher, harder and brighter.

controls.label: Instability
controls.hint: A healthy, steady core to one that lurches and growls.

controls.label: Conduits
controls.hint: Bare rumble to a singing, swirling chord over it.

controls.label: Hull
controls.hint: A cramped crawlway to a cavernous steel hold.

controls.label: Systems
controls.hint: Dead consoles and still air to a busy, hissing, pinging room.

patch.name: Bird tweet
patch.description: A robin-sized songbird on a branch ten metres away, one phrase: four clear whistled notes that each swoop down and flick up (every 115 ms, drifting higher), then a fast dry trill of a dozen chips from 520 ms that tumbles down and stops at 800 ms. The wood answers softly.

tracks.note: The whistled notes: a nearly pure tone from the syrinx with a fast swoop in each note. The second voice of the syrinx adds a faint shimmer above.
The rattle that ends the phrase: quick falling chips at about 30 a second, the whole run sliding down a third.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A tiny wren to a blackbird: lower, rounder notes.

controls.label: Tempo
controls.hint: A lazy song to a hurried one.

controls.label: Melody
controls.hint: Every note the same, to a phrase that climbs and wanders.

controls.label: Trill
controls.hint: Whistles only, to a long rattle at the end.

controls.label: Distance
controls.hint: On your windowsill to far off in the wood.

patch.name: Critter chirp
patch.description: A palm-sized furry critter asking a question: two quick squeaks from a tiny throat, "pri-rip?", the second one higher and curling up at the end (0 and 130 ms, each about 90 ms), with a fast throat flutter, then a wet little sniff at 330 ms. Close, dry, in a burrow.

tracks.note: The voice: a tiny throat (size 0.42) squeaking twice. The pitch curve is the question mark; the flutter makes it furry, not a whistle.
A short wet sniff after the question: breath only, through the same small throat. Mute it and the critter is less alive.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A mouse-sized squeaker to a fat guinea pig: lower and rounder.

controls.label: Question
controls.hint: How far the second squeak jumps up: flat and bored to a startled "eep?".

controls.label: Flutter
controls.hint: The purring roll in the throat: a clean peep to a rolled "prrr".

controls.label: Sniff
controls.hint: The wet sniff after the squeaks, from none to a snuffly nose.

patch.name: Ghostly moan
patch.description: Something that used to be a person, sighing in an empty stone church: a breathy "oooh" with no chest in it rises a third over the first second, trembles, and sinks away by 2.6 s, doubled by a second voice a little out of tune. Before it, a whisper is sucked in backwards, and a draught whistles thinly through a keyhole above everything. Most of what you hear is the building.

tracks.note: The voice: slack folds, half breath, vowel drifting between "oo" and "oh". The slow vibrato that fades in is the sorrow.
A whispered breath played backwards, so it swells and is cut off just as the moan begins: the "wrong" detail that makes it a ghost.
Cold air through a gap: noise ringing in a narrow tube whose pitch follows the moan a fifth above, very quiet.

controls.label: Sorrow
controls.hint: A flat, empty sigh to a wailing lament: wider pitch arc and tremble.

controls.label: Voice
controls.hint: A lost child, a woman, to a hollow old man.

controls.label: Breath
controls.hint: A sung tone to almost nothing but air.

controls.label: Draught
controls.hint: The thin whistle of cold air around the voice.

controls.label: Beyond
controls.hint: In the room with you, to far away on the other side.

patch.name: Insect fly-by
patch.description: A fat bumblebee crossing in front of your face from left to right at five metres a second, passing 30 cm from the nose at 1.1 s: 170 wing beats a second, never quite steady, the buzz bending down as it passes and fading into the garden by 2.3 s. Stereo.

tracks.note: The wing beat: a narrow pulse wave that wanders in pitch and flutters in level as the insect corrects its flight, moved past the listener.
The papery rustle of the wings themselves: thin noise chopped at the wing rate, heard only when it is close.

controls.label: Insect
controls.hint: A whining mosquito, through a housefly, to a heavy bumblebee.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: Drifting past to zipping by: a bigger, quicker pitch drop.

controls.label: Closeness
controls.hint: Across the garden to brushing your ear.

controls.label: Nerves
controls.hint: A calm cruise to a frantic, zigzagging buzz.

patch.name: Kaiju roar
patch.description: A skyscraper-sized monster roaring over a city, made the way the classic one was: a resined glove dragged down a slack bass string, slowed down. A metallic shriek climbs for 400 ms, holds and wavers, then falls away over two seconds, on top of a chest roar an octave and more below it and a blast of air. The roar hits the far buildings and comes back 180 ms later.

tracks.note: The signature: a bowed, gritty string with a pitch arc, pushed through a giant mouth. This is what makes it a kaiju and not a lion.
The body under the shriek: a kaiju-sized throat growling at 50 to 70 Hz with harmonics up to 400 Hz so laptops still get the weight.
The air leaving a mouth the size of a bus: a noise swell that peaks with the shriek and outlasts it a little.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A dinosaur to a monster that blocks out the sky: everything drops and slows.

controls.label: Shriek
controls.hint: How much of the metallic scream rides on top: a deep bellow to a piercing screech.

controls.label: Rage
controls.hint: A tired call to a furious, distorted, air-blasting roar.

controls.label: Distance
controls.hint: Standing under it to hearing it from across the bay: more city echo, less top.

patch.name: Monster growl
patch.description: A bear-sized beast warning you off from the back of its den: a chest-deep growl that swells for 300 ms, opens from "oo" to "ah" as the lips pull back around 600 ms, rattles there, then sinks and closes by 1.7 s. Hot breath hisses through the teeth the whole time. Heard from three metres in a rock chamber.

tracks.note: The growl itself: a big throat with period-doubled folds (growl) and a slow rattle in level. Pitch rises with the threat and sags at the end.
Air through wet teeth: pink noise shaped by the same mouth opening. It carries the growl on small speakers.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A big dog to something that fills the cave: deeper chest, longer throat.

controls.label: Anger
controls.hint: A low warning rumble to a torn, snarling threat with bared teeth.

controls.label: Length
controls.hint: A short grunt of a growl to a long drawn-out one.

controls.label: Den
controls.hint: Right at your ear to deep inside an echoing rock chamber.

patch.name: Robot creature chatter
patch.description: A knee-high maintenance droid with opinions: about 0.9 s of burbling electronic speech, a dozen syllables of unstable tone that jump in pitch like words, squeezed through a small plastic speaker-mouth, ending on a rising two-note "bee-woop?" at 950 ms. Its head servo twitches as it finishes. Close, in a corridor.

tracks.note: The speech: two cross-modulating oscillators whose pitch is thrown to a new value 13 times a second, each syllable a little chaotic. Seeds change what it says.
The sign-off: two clean notes, the second sliding up. It turns noise into a sentence with a meaning.
The head tilting as it asks: a small geared motor, 160 ms. Gives the voice a body.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A pocket-sized bot to a barrel-shaped one: lower voice, bigger mouth.

controls.label: Talk speed
controls.hint: Slow, deliberate words to an excited gabble.

controls.label: Expression
controls.hint: A monotone drone to wild leaps of pitch.

controls.label: Glitch
controls.hint: A healthy clean voice to a damaged, crackling one.

controls.label: Servo
controls.hint: How loudly its head motor twitches at the end.

patch.name: Slime squelch
patch.description: A fist-sized blob of slime dropping onto a stone floor and pulling itself together: a soft rubbery splat at 0, the wet suck of its skin peeling off the stone from 40 to 260 ms (a mouth-like "shhluck" that closes), and a dozen fat bubbles popping inside it until about 350 ms. Close and dry.

tracks.note: The body landing: a dead rubber skin hit softly. No ring, only a round thump at 100 to 200 Hz.
The squelch: wet noise through a small mouth that goes from open to closed, so it says "shluck". The vowel sweep is the stickiness.
Air pockets popping in the goo: rising-pitch drops, biggest first. They make it thick liquid, not water.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A drip of goo to a bucket-sized blob: lower, fatter bubbles and a heavier splat.

controls.label: Stickiness
controls.hint: A quick wet slap to a long, reluctant peel.

controls.label: Bubbles
controls.hint: Smooth jelly to a fizzing, popping mass.

controls.label: Wetness
controls.hint: Thick and dull to thin, glistening and splashy.

patch.name: Door latch click
patch.description: An interior door pulled shut by its handle until the latch catches. 0 ms: the angled latch bolt meets the strike plate and is pushed back with a short brassy scrape of 45 ms; at 50 ms its spring fires it into the hole in the frame with the click itself, small, hard and metallic; 4 ms after that the door leaf meets the stop and the whole door gives one soft, deep wooden bump; a faint zing of the handle spring settling.

tracks.note: The bolt riding over the strike plate: a short brass scrape, speeding up.
The click: the sprung bolt snapping into the frame.
The door meeting its stop: one soft deep bump from the whole leaf and frame.
The handle spring settling: a faint short zing.

controls.label: Door
controls.hint: A light hollow door that pats shut, to a heavy solid one that thuds.

controls.label: Push
controls.hint: Eased shut so only the latch speaks, or pushed firmly home.

controls.label: Latch
controls.hint: A small cupboard catch to a big old mortice lock.

controls.label: Spring
controls.hint: A dead latch, or a rattly handle whose spring zings.

controls.label: Room
controls.hint: Dry, or an empty room.

patch.name: Metal hatch slams
patch.description: A watertight steel hatch on a ship swung shut and dogged, from inside the compartment. 0 to 300 ms: the hatch swings on a dry hinge with a rising metallic groan; at 320 ms the door meets its frame, a heavy boxy boom with a hard steel edge, its rubber seal stopping it ringing for long; at 520 ms the locking lever is thrown and the dog lands with a second, smaller, brighter clank; the steel compartment rings round all of it.

tracks.note: The dry hinge as the hatch swings: a rough, rising metallic moan that stops at the slam.
The slam: a thick steel door as a closed box, hit all along its edge; the seal damps the highs.
Steel edge on steel frame: the hard bright clack on the front of the boom.
The locking lever thrown home 200 ms later: a smaller, harder clank and its rebound.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A locker door to a vault: lower, longer, heavier.

controls.label: Hinge
controls.hint: A greased hinge that swings silently, or a rusted one that groans.

controls.label: Seal
controls.hint: A rubber gasket that deadens it to a thunk, or bare steel on steel that clangs.

controls.label: Lock
controls.hint: Just the slam, or the locking lever clanking home after it.

controls.label: Compartment
controls.hint: On an open deck, or sealed inside a steel hull.

patch.name: Wooden door creaks open
patch.description: A heavy old panelled door pushed slowly open on dry iron hinges, in a stone-floored hallway. The hinge pin sticks and slips: a train of tiny clicks so fast it becomes a groan. It unsticks with a quick stutter, settles to a rough purr of about 40 slips a second, climbs to a whining 175 as the door speeds up through the middle of its swing, falters, then drops back to separate ticks as the door comes to rest after 1.8 s. The door panel is the loudspeaker for the hinge: it gives the groan its woody, vowel-like colour.

tracks.note: Stick-slip at the hinge pin: one click per slip, the rate following the door speed. Through the door panel (two formant-like resonances).
The door leaf itself flexing: quiet low knocks of the panel as the hinge jerks.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: Opened inch by inch, or swung open in half a second.

controls.label: Hinge
controls.hint: A deep groaning castle door to a thin squeaking cupboard hinge.

controls.label: Rust
controls.hint: A hinge that purrs evenly, or a rusted one that stutters and catches.

controls.label: Door
controls.hint: Just the hinge, or a big panel that sings along with it.

controls.label: Hallway
controls.hint: Close and dry, or echoing down a stone hall.

patch.name: Big boom with debris
patch.description: A fuel depot goes up a hundred metres away. The explosion is built the way film sound does it: a sharp, complete bang recorded 'small' (a crack, a drum-like thump and a burst of fire noise, 300 ms long) is played back at 40 % speed, so everything in it becomes slow, low and enormous: a 30 ms crack, a boom that takes most of a second to fall, and fire that roars for two. From 400 ms the debris comes down: big pieces first, clattering and bouncing, then smaller ones for three seconds.

tracks.note: The crack and fireball, before slowing: bright noise with a fast-closing filter. Varispeed turns its 0.35 s into nearly a second of roar.
The body: a drum skin struck hard, pitched like a tom, then slowed by the same factor so it lands at 60 to 150 Hz with its overtones intact.
What comes down: individual pieces of rubble, each a little struck object, big ones first (size ties pitch to level and ring).
One large piece that lands late and bounces to rest: a dented metal sheet. A single identifiable event in the rain of rubble.

controls.label: Scale
controls.hint: A car backfire-sized bang to a slow, city-shaking detonation.

controls.label: Fire
controls.hint: A dry thud, or a long roaring fireball over it.

controls.label: Debris
controls.hint: Nothing thrown, to a long rain of wreckage.

controls.label: Wreckage
controls.hint: What is falling.

controls.label: Open air
controls.hint: Close and dry to rolling across a wide open site.

patch.name: Distant explosion in a valley
patch.description: Artillery landing four kilometres away on the far side of a mountain valley, heard from a hillside on a still evening. There is no crack: the air has taken everything above 600 Hz. What arrives is a soft, round thump at 90 Hz, felt as much as heard, and then the valley playing with it: the first echo off the near slope 700 ms later, another off the far wall, each darker and softer, merging into a low roll that wanders and takes six seconds to die.

tracks.note: The blast as it arrives: a very large membrane hit with a soft beater. No transient on purpose. Tube drive adds harmonics at 180 and 270 Hz so the thump exists on small speakers.
The rumble that follows the thump along the ground: brown noise, slowly heaving (wander on level and cutoff), never above 300 Hz.

controls.label: Distance
controls.hint: A kilometre off, with some knock left in it, to far beyond the ridge: only a soft pressure.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A mortar round to a magazine going up.

controls.label: Echoes
controls.hint: Flat open plain, one thump, to a deep valley that answers again and again.

controls.label: Valley width
controls.hint: A narrow gorge with quick echoes to a wide basin with slow ones.

controls.label: Rumble
controls.hint: Just the thump and its echoes, or a long ground-rolling rumble after it.

patch.name: Firework rocket
patch.description: A rocket at a town display, watched from the square. 0 ms: the fuse lights and it leaves the tube with a short fizzing 'fsst'. 0 to 1.1 s: it climbs, screaming: a whistle (noise in a narrow pipe) that rises from 1.4 to 3.3 kHz with a fast warble and thins as it gets higher and farther. 1.1 to 1.3 s: silence. 1.3 s: the shell bursts 150 m up, a deep 'boomp' with a soft crack on it, already rounded by the distance. Then the stars: two seconds of crackling as they burn out, drifting down, and the bang coming back off the buildings.

tracks.note: Lift-off: a fizz of violet noise and a small hollow thump from the mortar tube.
The screamer: noise forced through a tube resonator that climbs. The 26 Hz warble is the whistle composition burning unevenly; the gain curve is the rocket getting farther away.
The shell breaking: a soft-edged boom high overhead. Membrane plus noise exciter gives thump and crack in one; the lowpass is 150 m of air.
The stars burning out: crackle that starts thick right after the burst and thins for two seconds, spread across the sky.

controls.label: Height
controls.hint: A low garden rocket, bursting soon and bright, to a big shell high up: a longer climb and a duller, later boom.

controls.label: Shell size
controls.hint: A small pop of colour to a chest-thumping aerial shell.

controls.label: Whistle
controls.hint: A silent climb, or a loud screaming one.

controls.label: Crackle
controls.hint: A plain burst, or a long glittering crackle of stars.

controls.label: Town
controls.hint: Open field to a square ringed with buildings throwing the bang back.

patch.name: Grenade
patch.description: A fragmentation grenade bursting in soft earth twenty metres off, in open country with a treeline. 0 ms: the detonation crack, hard and clipped. 3 ms: the blast body, a pressure wave that drops from 250 Hz to 75 Hz in 150 ms, overdriven so its harmonics carry on small speakers, with a ragged burst of dark noise as the ground lifts. 80 to 900 ms: steel fragments ring off stones as they land and clods of dirt patter down, thinning out. The treeline returns a soft roll.

tracks.note: Detonation: 10 ms of clipped white noise. Sets the scale: high explosive, not a firework.
The pressure wave: a falling sine, folded hard so it is a thick buzz-thump and not a kick drum. Weight at 100 to 300 Hz comes from the drive.
The ground lifting: dark noise with a closing filter, uneven because of the wander. Fills between crack and thump.
Steel splinters hitting stones: a few bright metal pings scattered through the fall-out.
Clods and soil raining back: dull, low ticks, more of them and for longer than the fragments.

controls.label: Charge
controls.hint: A flash-bang's thump to a satchel charge: lower, longer, heavier.

controls.label: Punch
controls.hint: A soft whump to a chest-hitting, distorted slam.

controls.label: Shrapnel
controls.hint: A plain blast, or steel pinging off everything.

controls.label: Dirt
controls.hint: Hard ground, nothing thrown, to a fountain of soil coming down.

controls.label: Roll
controls.hint: Flat and dry, or echoing back off a far treeline.

patch.name: Firecracker pop
patch.description: A single firecracker going off on a pavement three metres away. 0 ms: the crack, 4 ms of full-band noise as the paper tube bursts. 1 ms: the tube itself, a short hollow cardboard 'pok' at 480 Hz that gives the bang its small size. 15 to 250 ms: shreds of paper and grit scatter on the ground. 55 ms: one hard echo off the house across the street, duller, then a short street tail.

tracks.note: The burst: as short and bright as possible. Everything else is context for these 4 ms.
The paper tube: a cardboard pipe has almost no ring, just a hollow knock. This is what says 'small and paper' rather than 'gun'.
Paper and grit landing: sparse dry ticks, thinning out.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A toy cap, a tiny snap, to a fat banger with a hollow thump.

controls.label: Snap
controls.hint: A dull damp pop to an ear-stinging crack.

controls.label: Shreds
controls.hint: Paper and grit raining down afterwards.

controls.label: Street
controls.hint: Open field, no echo, to a narrow alley slapping it back.

patch.name: Footstep: leather shoe on concrete
patch.description: One step of a hard-soled leather shoe on a polished concrete corridor floor. 0 ms: the stacked leather heel lands with a short, hard, slightly hollow tock; 95 ms later the sole rolls down with a softer, duller pat and a faint scuff of grit under it; the corridor gives each a short hard slap. Use the variations for a walk.

tracks.note: Heel strike: a small hard block (the heel) on stone.
The floor answering: a dead stone thump that gives the step its weight.
The sole rolling down 95 ms after the heel: leather pat and a little grit scuff.

controls.label: Shoe
controls.hint: A soft sneaker that pads, to a dress shoe, to a hard stiletto click.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A light quick step to a heavy stomp.

controls.label: Pace
controls.hint: A slow stroll with the heel and sole far apart, to a run where they land together.

controls.label: Scuff
controls.hint: A clean placed step, or a dragged sole on a gritty floor.

controls.label: Corridor
controls.hint: Dry, or a long empty corridor.

patch.name: Footstep: creaky wooden floor
patch.description: One slow step on an old floorboard in a quiet house at night. 0 ms: a socked heel lands with a low hollow thump, the board booming over the space under it; from 50 ms, as the weight comes on, the board rubs on its nail and creaks: a stick-slip groan of about 300 ms that starts near 220 Hz, sags, and ends in a few separate ticks as it stops. Use the variations for a walk.

tracks.note: The step: a soft heel on a long plank over a hollow.
The board rubbing on its nail under the weight: wood scraped over evenly spaced ridges, slowing to single ticks.

controls.label: Creak
controls.hint: A sound board that only thumps, or a loud long complaint.

controls.label: Board
controls.hint: A thick old beam that groans low, to a thin dry board that squeaks.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A cat-light step to a heavy man.

controls.label: Shoe
controls.hint: Bare feet and socks, or hard boots that knock.

controls.label: House
controls.hint: Close and dry, or an empty room.

patch.name: Footstep: gravel
patch.description: One step of a walking boot on a loose gravel drive, outdoors. 0 ms: the heel digs in and a hundred pea-sized stones grind and click against each other for 90 ms; 80 ms later the ball of the foot rolls forward with a second, longer and finer crunch as stones are pushed away; a soft low thump of the packed ground sits under the heel. No echo: open air. Use the variations for a walk.

tracks.note: Heel crunch: a dense burst of small stones, coarse and loud.
Toe roll: a longer, finer, quieter crunch as the foot pushes off.
The packed earth under the stones: a soft thump so the step has a body.

controls.label: Stones
controls.hint: Fine grit and sand to coarse river pebbles that clack.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A child tiptoeing to a soldier with a pack.

controls.label: Pace
controls.hint: A slow careful step with a long toe roll, to a run that lands all at once.

controls.label: Wet
controls.hint: Dry dusty gravel, crisp and bright, or rain-soaked and dull.

patch.name: Footstep: metal grate
patch.description: One step of a work boot on a steel catwalk grating in a ship's engine room. 0 ms: the rubber sole lands and the loose panel clanks down onto its frame; the grating rings with a dense, sour clang of many bars for a third of a second; 35 ms after the step the panel bounces once more on its clips with a smaller rattle; the steel compartment rings back.

tracks.note: The grating: a welded lattice, struck by a rubber sole. Dense, dented, short.
The loose panel hitting its frame: steel on steel, then a rebound 35 ms later.
The boot itself: a soft rubber thud under the clang.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A light quick step to a heavy armoured stomp.

controls.label: Loose
controls.hint: A welded deck that only rings, or a loose panel that clatters on its frame.

controls.label: Ring
controls.hint: Thick damped plate that clunks, to thin grating that sings.

controls.label: Panel
controls.hint: A small stair tread to a long span of walkway.

controls.label: Compartment
controls.hint: Open air gantry, or deep inside a steel hull.

patch.name: Footstep: puddle splash
patch.description: One step of a rubber boot into a shallow street puddle. 0 ms: the sole slaps the water with a flat wet smack; under it the boot meets the asphalt with a dull thud; the water thrown out sideways lands as a spray of droplets from 40 to 400 ms, big blooping drops first, fine patter last; a hollow gulp as water closes in round the boot. Use the variations for a walk.

tracks.note: Sole on water: a flat burst of noise that closes down fast, like a hand slapping a bath.
The thrown water landing back: droplets and bubbles, pitch rising as they get smaller.
Water closing round the boot: a hollow, rising bloop.
The street under the water.

controls.label: Depth
controls.hint: A wet pavement to an ankle-deep puddle: more gulp, lower and longer.

controls.label: Splash
controls.hint: A careful step, or a jump that throws water everywhere.

controls.label: Stomp
controls.hint: A soft wade in, or a hard flat slap.

controls.label: Street
controls.hint: Open and dry-sounding, or between wet walls.

patch.name: Footstep: snow
patch.description: One step in ankle-deep cold snow on a still winter day. No impact at all: the boot presses down over 180 ms and the snow compacts with a creaking, squeaking crunch that swells as the weight comes on and stops when the foot is down; under it a soft muffled whumpf; then 60 ms of fine crystals falling back into the print. Close, dead, no echo: snow swallows everything. Use the variations for a walk.

tracks.note: Snow compacting: crackling noise through a narrow resonance that slides down as the snow packs. The creak of cold snow.
The crust and grains breaking under the sole: many small dull ticks, thickest in the middle of the step.
The weight going into the snow pack: a soft low push, no attack.
Loose crystals falling back into the footprint after the step.

controls.label: Cold
controls.hint: Wet slushy snow that squelches dully, to dry powder at -20 that squeaks.

controls.label: Depth
controls.hint: A dusting over hard ground, or knee-deep drifts: a longer, lower press.

controls.label: Crust
controls.hint: Soft fresh snow, or an icy crust that cracks under the boot.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A light step to a heavy one that sinks.

patch.name: Body punch
patch.description: A film-style punch to the ribs, miked close. -45 ms: the sleeve cuts the air, a short swish rising in pitch; 0 ms: the fist lands, a wet leathery smack over a deep, dead thump of flesh (the chest gives, so the thump sags in pitch), with a dull knuckle-on-bone knock inside it; all of it is over in 150 ms, squeezed hard like a movie fight.

tracks.note: The arm coming: 45 ms of sleeve and air before the hit, cut off by it.
The thump: a soft dead mass, hit with a padded fist. The pitch sags as the body gives.
Skin and cloth: the wet slap on top, the part laptop speakers carry.
Knuckles on ribs: a short woody knock inside the thump.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A jab to a heavyweight body blow: lower, longer, fatter.

controls.label: Smack
controls.hint: A muffled hit through a coat, or a bare wet slap.

controls.label: Bone
controls.hint: All soft tissue, or a crack of knuckle on rib.

controls.label: Swing
controls.hint: No wind-up, or a big telegraphed swing you hear coming.

patch.name: Cardboard box dropped
patch.description: A half-full moving box dropped from knee height onto a laminate floor. 0 ms: it lands on one bottom edge with a dead papery whump; at 95 ms it tips flat with a second, softer and lower thump; from 20 ms the things inside (books, loose cutlery) slide and knock against the walls for a third of a second. No ring anywhere: cardboard eats it.

tracks.note: The box: a dead cardboard cavity. Two events: the edge lands, then it tips flat.
The flat face slapping the floor: papery mid noise, on the second landing.
What is inside, sliding and knocking the walls.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A shoebox to a wardrobe carton.

controls.label: Contents
controls.hint: Empty, or packed with things that slide and knock.

controls.label: Hard stuff
controls.hint: Soft clothes and books inside, or cutlery and tins.

controls.label: Drop
controls.hint: Set down gently to dropped from the shoulder: harder, with a livelier tumble.

patch.name: Coin dropped and settling
patch.description: A large coin dropped a hand-width onto a wooden table top. 0 ms: it lands on its edge with a bright ring; it hops four or five times, faster and faster and a little wild because it is spinning; near 600 ms it falls onto its face and wobbles round its rim, the rattle speeding up and rising in pitch as it flattens, until it stops dead at about 1.4 s. The table knocks softly under the first hits.

tracks.note: The coin bouncing on its edge: one small metal disc, each hop sooner and softer.
The spin-down: the coin rolling round its rim, faster and higher until it lies flat.
The table top under the first hits: a soft wooden knock that gives it a place.

controls.label: Coin
controls.hint: A tiny thin coin that tinks to a heavy silver dollar.

controls.label: Height
controls.hint: Slipped from the fingers, or dropped from standing: longer hops.

controls.label: Spin
controls.hint: Lands flat and stops, or spins down in a long rising rattle.

controls.label: Table
controls.hint: Stone counter with no voice, or a hollow wooden table that knocks.

patch.name: Knock on a wooden door
patch.description: Knuckles on a panelled interior door, heard from the hallway side: three raps about 170 ms apart, uneven as a hand is, the second the firmest. Each rap is a bony knuckle click and then the door panel answering as a wide shallow wooden box; the room behind the door gives a short muffled bloom.

tracks.note: The door panel: a thin wooden box that booms low and dies fast.
Bone on wood: the small hard click on top of each rap.

controls.label: Knocks
controls.hint: One rap to five.

controls.label: Urgency
controls.hint: A slow polite tap to fast hard pounding.

controls.label: Door
controls.hint: A thin hollow-core door that booms, to a thick oak one that barely answers.

controls.label: Room behind
controls.hint: Nothing behind the door, or an empty room that answers.

patch.name: Giant metal slam
patch.description: A blast door the size of a house dropping shut at the far end of an empty hangar. 0 ms: thousands of tons of plate steel meet the sill with a grinding, crumbling crash, not a clean clang; a boom near 60 Hz rolls under it for two seconds; the plate keeps groaning and shimmering as its huge slow modes beat; from 150 ms loosened bolts and rust rain down for a second; the hangar answers 60 ms later with a long dark roar.

tracks.note: The door: an enormous dented steel plate set off by a rough crushing contact, its modes beating slowly.
The floor and the air: a pitchless boom that carries the weight, with harmonics so small speakers show it.
Bolts, scale and rust shaken loose, falling for a second.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A shipping container door to a dam gate.

controls.label: Distance
controls.hint: Standing under it, or hearing it from the far end of the hall: more roar, less edge.

controls.label: Debris
controls.hint: A clean close, or bolts and rust raining after it.

controls.label: Rust
controls.hint: New machined steel that tolls, or a corroded wreck that crunches and dies sooner.

controls.label: Hall
controls.hint: A big workshop to an endless cavern.

patch.name: Two glasses clink
patch.description: Two wine glasses touched rim to rim in a toast, close to the ear at a dinner table. The two bowls are slightly different sizes, so two clear notes a wide third apart ring together; the second glass speaks 3 ms after the first; each is not quite round, so its note shimmers; the wine inside dulls the top of the ring.

tracks.note: Your glass: the lower note.
Their glass: a little smaller and thinner, 3 ms late.
The contact itself: a dry glassy tick.

controls.label: Glass size
controls.hint: Shot glasses that tink to big balloon glasses that sing low.

controls.label: Fill
controls.hint: Empty crystal that rings on, or full glasses whose ring is short and dull.

controls.label: Toast
controls.hint: A careful touch to an enthusiastic clack.

controls.label: Mismatch
controls.hint: A matched pair on one note, or two odd glasses far apart.

controls.label: Room
controls.hint: Dry at the ear, or across a dining room.

patch.name: Glass shatters
patch.description: A window pane broken by a thrown stone, heard from inside a kitchen. 0 ms: the pane cracks with one hard, noisy clang; from 15 ms the pieces let go, a dense shower of shards that thins out over a second, the big pieces low and loud, the splinters high and faint; from 250 ms the first shards reach the tiled floor and skitter and tinkle to rest.

tracks.note: The pane giving way: a sheet of glass excited by a rough, crumbling hit.
The stone meeting the pane in its wooden frame: the low knock that gives the break a body.
The pieces: a burst of small glass plates, thinning out.
Shards landing on tiles and settling: sparse bright pings, late.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A drinking glass to a shop window.

controls.label: Pieces
controls.hint: A clean break into a few big pieces, or an explosion of splinters.

controls.label: Floor
controls.hint: Carpet that swallows the pieces, or hard tiles they dance on.

controls.label: Force
controls.hint: A crack that lets go slowly, or a violent smash.

controls.label: Room
controls.hint: Dry, or a hard tiled room.

patch.name: Metal pipe struck
patch.description: A length of steel scaffolding pipe hanging from one hand, struck near its end with a wrench in a concrete garage. 0 ms: the steel-on-steel tick; from 2 ms the pipe rings on its bar modes, slightly out of round so every partial beats slowly; under it the air inside the pipe answers with a short hollow bonk; the garage returns a hard slap.

tracks.note: The pipe itself: a free steel bar hit near the end, slightly bent so the partials beat.
The air column inside: a wrench tick ringing a hollow tube, the "bonk" that says pipe and not rod.
The first 3 ms of steel on steel.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A short offcut that pings to a long heavy pole that tolls.

controls.label: Strike
controls.hint: A rubber boot heel to a steel wrench: duller and rounder, or brighter with a hard tick.

controls.label: Grip
controls.hint: Hanging free and singing, or clamped in a fist so the ring chokes at once.

controls.label: Hollow
controls.hint: A solid bar, or a wide pipe whose air column bonks.

controls.label: Garage
controls.hint: Dry and close, or ringing off the concrete walls.

patch.name: Rock on rock
patch.description: A fist-sized river stone thrown down onto a boulder in a dry gorge. 0 ms: a hard, pitchless stony clack, both lumps answering at once with their own irregular modes, over in 60 ms; from 8 ms a few chips and grit skip off; about 170 ms later the far wall of the gorge sends the clack back, darker, and again fainter comes back.

tracks.note: The thrown stone: a small irregular lump, hit hard.
The boulder it lands on: bigger, lower, deader, 1 ms behind.
Chips and grit skipping away after the hit.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: Two pebbles clicking to boulders colliding.

controls.label: Force
controls.hint: A tap to a hard throw that knocks chips off.

controls.label: Stone
controls.hint: Soft crumbly sandstone to glassy flint that clicks.

controls.label: Gorge
controls.hint: No echo, or a rock wall that throws the clack back.

controls.label: Wall distance
controls.hint: A wall 15 metres off to one 100 metres away: a later echo.

patch.name: Rubber ball bounces to rest
patch.description: A solid rubber bouncy ball dropped from waist height onto a wooden gym floor. First bounce at 0 ms, the next about 310 ms later, each gap about four fifths of the last, each hit softer, until the bounces run together into a short buzz and stop near 2 s. Every bounce is the same ball: a round, pitched "pock" with the hollow floor answering under it, in a big empty gym.

tracks.note: The ball: one rubber sphere bouncing, each gap a fixed fraction of the last.

controls.label: Height
controls.hint: Dropped from a hand-width, or thrown down from overhead: longer gaps, more bounces.

controls.label: Bounciness
controls.hint: A dead ball that stops in three hops, or a super ball that will not quit.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A marble-sized super ball to a basketball.

controls.label: Floor
controls.hint: Solid concrete, or a hollow wooden floor that booms with each bounce.

controls.label: Gym
controls.hint: A small room to an empty sports hall.

patch.name: Heavy sack thud
patch.description: A 25 kg sack of grain dropped off a shoulder onto the plank floor of a barn. 0 ms: a soft, wide whump with no click at all, the burlap spreading for 40 ms rather than hitting; the floor planks boom once underneath around 100 Hz and its neighbours; from 30 ms the grain inside slumps with a short dry hiss; a little dust and a wooden room around it.

tracks.note: The sack landing: dark noise that opens and closes in 60 ms. A spread, not a hit.
The planks: a big wooden cavity kicked by something soft, the pitch of the thud.
The contents slumping after the landing: a dry hiss of small grains.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A pillow to a body: lower, longer, more floor.

controls.label: Floor
controls.hint: Packed earth that gives nothing back, or a hollow stage that booms.

controls.label: Filling
controls.hint: A solid lump, or loose grain that hisses as it settles.

controls.label: Slap
controls.hint: A soft slump, or a flat landing with a leathery slap.

controls.label: Barn
controls.hint: Dry and close, or in a big wooden room.

patch.name: Trash can kicked
patch.description: A dented galvanised trash can kicked hard in a back alley. 0 ms: the boot lands on the thin steel wall with a dull bong (rubber sole, so no tick); the wall is creased, so the clang is sour and uneven and buckles downward in pitch for the first 60 ms; from 30 ms the loose lid chatters on the rim for half a second, slowing down; brick walls throw back a short hard echo.

tracks.note: The can wall: thin dented sheet steel hit by a soft boot. The pitch sag is the sheet buckling.
The loose lid rattling on the rim: a rolling chatter that slows to a stop.
The empty drum: the low breath of the can body under the clang.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A paint tin to an oil drum.

controls.label: Kick
controls.hint: A nudge with a sneaker to a full swing with a steel toecap.

controls.label: Dents
controls.hint: A new can with a clean clang to battered junk.

controls.label: Lid
controls.hint: No lid, or a loose one that chatters on.

controls.label: Alley
controls.hint: Open yard to a narrow brick alley.

patch.name: Dark curse
patch.description: A curse is laid in a crypt. 0 to 900 ms: a whisper that is sucked backwards into the caster's mouth (breathy syllables recorded forwards, played in reverse, so each one swells and stops dead). 900 ms: the curse lands. A huge throat, something far bigger than a person, lets out a falling growl from 'ah' down to a closed 'oo', its pitch sinking a fifth over 1.2 s, ring-modulated at 41 Hz so it rattles. Over it a cracked iron bell tolls once, a little flat. The crypt keeps both for three seconds.

tracks.note: The incantation, reversed: four whispered syllables (voice with no tone, only breath), each with its own vowel sweep. The reverse makes them inhale.
What answers: a giant throat growling down. Growl adds the octave-below snarl; the ring modulator makes it shake like something not alive.
The toll that marks it: a big cracked bell (dent), its modes beating slowly. 12 ms after the growl starts, so the two do not fuse.

controls.label: Menace
controls.hint: A petty hex to something enormous and very angry.

controls.label: Whisper
controls.hint: No incantation, or loud hissing syllables before it lands.

controls.label: Rattle
controls.hint: A living throat to a shuddering, undead buzz.

controls.label: Bell
controls.hint: No toll, or a great cracked bell over the growl.

controls.label: Crypt
controls.hint: Close in a small cell, or lost in a vast vault.

patch.name: Fireball
patch.description: A fireball lit in the caster's hand and thrown. 0 ms: ignition, a soft 'whoomp' as the air catches (low noise opening quickly from 150 Hz to 2 kHz, with a pressure thump under it). 0 to 1.3 s: the ball roars and flutters like a torch swung through the air, and it travels away from you at 28 m/s, so the roar drops in pitch and dulls. All the way it spits and crackles: embers popping off, thinning as it goes.

tracks.note: Ignition: the pressure thump. A big soft membrane, not a sine drop, so it sounds like air and not a kick drum.
The flame: pink noise whose filter flutters at random (wander plus a fast random tremolo) is what makes it burn instead of hiss. Doppler carries it away.
Sparks and pops: sharp, uneven, never regular. Without them it is wind.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A candle-sized firebolt to a cart-sized ball of flame.

controls.label: Crackle
controls.hint: Smooth clean flame to a spitting, popping blaze.

controls.label: Flutter
controls.hint: A steady jet to a wildly guttering torch.

controls.label: Throw
controls.hint: Held burning in the hand, or hurled away fast.

controls.label: Ignition
controls.hint: How hard it catches at the start.

patch.name: Healing spell
patch.description: A healer lays hands on a wound in a stone chapel. A small choir of soft voices breathes in on 'oo' and opens to 'ah' over 1.2 s, rising a tone as the light comes. Across it a harp runs upward, eight nylon strings plucked by a thumb in 600 ms. The warmth stays for a moment in the chapel and fades. Nothing sharp anywhere: it should feel like breathing out.

tracks.note: The warmth: real throats (voice model), soft tension, lots of breath. Chorus makes three singers of one.
A second, lower part a fifth below: body for small speakers, and it makes the choir a chord.
The gesture: a rising run, soft thumb plucks, slowing slightly toward the top.

controls.label: Length
controls.hint: A quick potion sip to a long, slow restoration.

controls.label: Voices
controls.hint: Children's choir, high and small, down to monks.

controls.label: Breath
controls.hint: Clear sung tone to an airy whispered sigh.

controls.label: Harp
controls.hint: Voices alone, or a bright run of strings across them.

controls.label: Chapel
controls.hint: A small quiet room to a tall stone nave.

patch.name: Ice spell crack
patch.description: A frost spell freezes a puddle solid and the ice splits. 0 to 550 ms: frost racing across the surface, a dry creaking scrape over a thin glassy sheet that speeds up and rises in pitch as the crystals close in. 560 ms: the sheet cracks, a hard, bright, short snap (a brittle ceramic-like plate, badly flawed), with a second smaller crack 70 ms later as the fracture runs. Then splinters skitter away on the ice for half a second, and a cold thin breath of air hangs over it.

tracks.note: Freezing: a scrape exciter on a glass plate. The ridge rate climbs, so the creak tightens. High damping keeps it dry: ice, not a wine glass.
The split: the loudest, shortest thing. A flawed ceramic plate hit at its edge with steel; the transient shaper makes it snap. Two events: the crack, and the fracture running on.
The thickness of the ice giving way under the crack: a dull stone knock at 170 Hz so the snap has weight on small speakers.
Shards skittering off across the ice after the crack: small glass pieces, big ones first.
Cold air: a thin high hiss that swells with the freeze and lingers. Makes the space feel frozen.

controls.label: Freeze time
controls.hint: An instant flash-freeze to a long creeping frost before the crack.

controls.label: Thickness
controls.hint: A thin brittle skin of ice to a thick slab that booms when it splits.

controls.label: Crack
controls.hint: A soft tick to a vicious snap.

controls.label: Splinters
controls.hint: A clean split, or shards scattering everywhere.

controls.label: Cold air
controls.hint: The thin frozen hiss over everything.

patch.name: Portal opening
patch.description: A doorway to somewhere else is forced open in a cave. It opens like a mouth: a deep buzzing drone (two sines grinding against each other) is shaped by a giant throat that moves from a closed 'oo' to a wide 'ah' over 1.8 s, growing as it goes. The rim spins: a rotor-like chop that starts at 3 beats a second and accelerates to 14 as the portal stabilises. Wind from the other side whistles through the gap, rising. After 2 s it holds open and the drone sinks back into the cave's long echo.

tracks.note: The portal's voice: cross-modulated sines for a thick, unstable buzz, then a formant filter with a huge throat. The vowel opening is the door opening.
Air from the other side: noise whistling through a tube whose note climbs as the gap widens. Wander keeps it gusting.
The edge burning: glittering metal shimmer from sparse crackles ringing a metal resonator. High, quiet, wide.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A keyhole rift to a gate a dragon could walk through.

controls.label: Opening time
controls.hint: Ripped open in a moment, or slowly prised apart.

controls.label: Spin
controls.hint: A still doorway to a hard-chopping vortex.

controls.label: Menace
controls.hint: A calm humming gate to a grinding, tearing wound in the air.

controls.label: Wind
controls.hint: How much air howls through from the other side.

patch.name: Sparkle pickup
patch.description: The hero's hand closes on a floating star shard. Five tiny glass notes run up a pentatonic scale in 240 ms, each one a small bowl-shaped chime with its partials beating, the last one ringing longest. As they rise, a puff of fairy dust goes up with them: a hundred faint pure pings from 3 to 11 kHz that climb and thin out over half a second. All of it in a bright plate so it glows instead of clicking.

tracks.note: The melody: glass-bowl ratios (1, 2.32, 4.25, 6.63), not a synth beep. Slightly uneven timing and velocities so a hand could have played it.
Fairy dust: separate pings, their range rising. This is what makes it magic and not a coin.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A big warm gem to a tiny glittering shard.

controls.label: Ring
controls.hint: Short muted ticks to long singing glass.

controls.label: Dust
controls.hint: Just the notes, or a whole cloud of glitter around them.

controls.label: Glow
controls.hint: Dry and close, or hanging in the air.

patch.name: Spell cast
patch.description: A mage throws an arcane bolt. 0 to 420 ms: energy is drawn into the staff, an unstable tone that wanders and climbs (an attractor being wound tighter), ringing a chord of sympathetic strings as it goes. 420 ms: release. The staff head rings like a struck bell with strange overtones, and the bolt leaves with a quick air tear that sweeps up and away. Then a short trail of rising sparks, and the string chord left hanging in a stone hall.

tracks.note: Drawing power: a Lorenz attractor, sped up and made less stable. The string resonator turns its buzz into a chord, so the wind-up is musical.
The cast itself: an FM bell with inharmonic ratios whose brightness dies faster than its level. Pitch kicks upward at the start, like something leaving.
Air torn by the bolt: starts 20 ms before the bell so the release has a leading edge.
What is left in the air: a few sparks that chirp upward.

controls.label: Charge time
controls.hint: An instant snap cast to a long, wound-up incantation.

controls.label: Power
controls.hint: A cantrip, small and high, to a heavy, clanging great spell.

controls.label: Wildness
controls.hint: Disciplined, tonal magic to raw crackling chaos.

controls.label: Whoosh
controls.hint: How much air the bolt tears on its way out.

controls.label: Hall
controls.hint: Outdoors and dry, or echoing in a stone chamber.

patch.name: Chain rattle
patch.description: Two metres of steel chain hauled off a hook and dropped in a heap on a concrete floor. 0 to 500 ms: the chain is dragged, links clinking against each other in a busy uneven patter, a few big links clanking low; around 550 ms the run thickens into a rush as it slides off; by 1 s the pile lands and the last links trickle down and settle with a few separate clinks. A bare concrete room.

tracks.note: The links hitting each other: many small steel rings, busy then a rush then a trickle.
The weight of it: slack loops and big links clanking low, fewer and louder.
The heap landing on concrete: a gritty low scrape under the rush.

controls.label: Gauge
controls.hint: A fine necklace chain that tinkles to ship's anchor chain that clanks.

controls.label: Busy
controls.hint: A lazy sway with single clinks, to a frantic shake.

controls.label: Length
controls.hint: A short jerk on the chain, or a long haul.

controls.label: Floor
controls.hint: Held in the air, or dragged and dumped on concrete.

controls.label: Cell
controls.hint: Dry, or a bare stone cell.

patch.name: Clock ticking (loop)
patch.description: A wooden mantel clock on a shelf in a quiet room, looping one second: tick at 0 ms, tock at 500 ms. Each beat is the escape wheel tooth dropping on a pallet, a tiny bright steel click, with a second fainter click 9 ms later as the pallet locks, and the clock's wooden case turning it into a soft hollow knock. The tock is a shade lower and duller than the tick, and the pair is not quite even, as in a clock slightly out of beat.

tracks.note: The escapement: steel tooth on steel pallet, drop then lock. Tick, then tock a shade lower.
The wooden case: the hollow knock that makes it a clock and not a relay.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A wristwatch held to the ear, to a grandfather clock in a hallway.

controls.label: Case
controls.hint: A bare movement, all click, or a resonant wooden case that knocks.

controls.label: Tick and tock
controls.hint: Two identical ticks, or a tick and a clearly lower tock.

controls.label: Room
controls.hint: At your ear, or across a silent room.

patch.name: Motor starting
patch.description: A big workshop extraction fan motor switched on at the wall. 0 ms: the contactor slams in with a heavy clunk that rings its steel cabinet; the motor lurches from standstill, growling under load, and climbs over 1.6 s to its running speed, the growl smoothing into a hum with a gear whine riding above it; it runs steadily for a moment, then fades as if you walked away.

tracks.note: The switchgear closing: a heavy relay clunk in a steel box.
The motor: from standstill to speed, load easing as it gets there.
The fan it drives: air building with the speed.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A desk fan to a ship's generator.

controls.label: Spin-up
controls.hint: Snaps up to speed, or takes its time getting a heavy flywheel moving.

controls.label: Age
controls.hint: New and smooth, or worn bearings that growl and wobble.

controls.label: Whine
controls.hint: A plain hum, or a gearbox that sings.

controls.label: Air
controls.hint: A bare motor, or one driving a big fan.

controls.label: Switch
controls.hint: A silent electronic start, or a contactor that slams.

patch.name: Ratchet
patch.description: A socket wrench swung back on its ratchet in a garage: fourteen pawl clicks in about half a second, starting quick and slowing a little as the wrist reaches the end of its swing, each one a hard steel click into a tooth with the hollow handle ringing shortly after it; uneven the way a hand is.

tracks.note: The pawl dropping into each tooth: a run of hard steel clicks, slowing slightly.
The gear body under the clicks: a low-mid knock so it is a tool, not a toy.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: A slow deliberate click, click, click to a fast zip.

controls.label: Clicks
controls.hint: A short flick of three teeth to a long swing.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A watchmaker's ratchet to a winch on a boat.

controls.label: Slow down
controls.hint: Even clicks like a machine, or a swing that runs out of travel.

controls.label: Handle
controls.hint: A solid tool, or a hollow chrome handle that rings with each click.

patch.name: Servo move
patch.description: A hobby-size robot arm servo turning its joint through 90 degrees and stopping, heard close. 0 ms: the gear train takes up its slack with a small tick; the motor whines up to speed in 60 ms, buzzes steadily, then strains and drops in pitch over the last 100 ms as it brakes against the load; at 480 ms it stops dead with a plastic clack of the gears settling. Its small plastic case makes it nasal.

tracks.note: The geared motor: spins up, holds, strains as it brakes.
The gears landing at the end of travel: a small hard plastic clack.
Backlash taken up at the start: a tiny tick.

controls.label: Travel
controls.hint: A small twitch to a long sweep of the arm.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: A slow precise crawl to a fast snap: higher whine.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A micro servo in a toy to an industrial arm joint.

controls.label: Strain
controls.hint: Moving nothing, or fighting a heavy load: rougher, buzzier.

controls.label: Stop
controls.hint: A soft controlled stop, or slamming into the end stop.

patch.name: Spring boing
patch.description: A doorstop spring flicked with a toe: the cartoon boing. 0 ms: the coil is bent and let go with a metallic twang; it whips back and forth so the pitch wobbles widely about seven times a second, the wobble dying over 600 ms while the whole note sags a little; the coil's overtones run away sharp of the pitch and chirp, the way spring reverbs do; a short plastic thunk from the skirting board it is screwed to.

tracks.note: The spring: a very stiff string, so its overtones go sharp and chirp. The LFO is the coil whipping about.
The wall it is screwed to: a short dull thunk at the flick.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A ballpoint pen spring to a car suspension coil.

controls.label: Wobble
controls.hint: A plain twang, or a wild whipping boing-oing-oing.

controls.label: Wobble speed
controls.hint: A slow drunken sway to a fast shiver.

controls.label: Coil
controls.hint: A tight wire that just twangs, to a loose slinky that chirps and splashes.

controls.label: Flick
controls.hint: A soft thumb to a hard fingernail: brighter twang.

patch.name: Toggle switch
patch.description: A chunky metal bat-handle toggle switch on an aluminium control panel, flipped up with a thumb. 0 ms: the lever passes centre with a faint plastic tick; 14 ms later the spring throws the contact home with a hard, bright snap; the panel it is bolted to answers with a short boxy "tok" that makes it sound mounted in something. Dry and close, like an aircraft cockpit.

tracks.note: The lever going over centre: the small pre-click.
The spring-loaded contact landing: a tiny steel bar, bright and very short.
The panel the switch is bolted to: a short boxy answer that gives it a size.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A tiny slide switch to a big knife-switch breaker.

controls.label: Throw
controls.hint: A crisp short-travel click, or a long lazy lever with a gap between tick and snap.

controls.label: Panel
controls.hint: A bare switch in the hand, or one mounted in a hollow console that knocks.

controls.label: Metal
controls.hint: A soft plastic rocker to a ringing all-metal toggle.

patch.name: Cloth swish
patch.description: A cotton jacket sleeve as an arm swings out and back: two brushes of fabric on fabric, the first 130 ms long and the answer 90 ms later softer and shorter. Each is thousands of fibres catching, so it is grainy rather than a hiss, and the weave gives it a faint zip. Very close, dry.

tracks.note: The fabric: a dense cloud of tiny noise grains whose rate swells and dies with each move. Grain size is the coarseness of the cloth.
The threads of the weave dragging past each other: a fast scrape on a dead cardboard-like surface, the faint "zip" inside the swish.

controls.label: Fabric
controls.hint: Silk, through cotton, to stiff canvas or leather: coarser, lower, louder weave.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: A slow drag to a quick flick.

controls.label: Return
controls.hint: One move only, to a full back-and-forth.

controls.label: Layers
controls.hint: A single thin sleeve to a heavy coat or cape: denser rustle.

patch.name: Jump take-off
patch.description: A runner in trainers jumping straight up from a wooden gym floor: the crouch loads the boards for 60 ms with a creak-less push (a soft double thump as heel then toe leave, 0 and 45 ms), the soles scuff grit as they twist off, and the body goes up through its own clothes with a short rising rush of air from 50 to 300 ms. No cartoon boing: the effort is in the push.

tracks.note: The floor taking the push: a wooden box struck softly twice, the toe higher and lighter than the heel. The physical part of the jump.
Rubber soles twisting on dust: a short burst of fine grit ticks at the toe-off.
The body rising: air and cloth rushing, its pitch climbing as the jumper accelerates away from the floor. This is what says "up".

controls.label: Effort
controls.hint: A little hop to an all-out leap: harder push, longer rush of air.

controls.label: Floor
controls.hint: What they jump from: boards, packed earth, a metal deck or stone.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A child to a knight in armour: lower, longer thumps.

controls.label: Grit
controls.hint: A clean floor to a dusty one that scuffs.

controls.label: Lift
controls.hint: How steeply the rush of air rises: a heavy heave to a light spring.

patch.name: Soft landing
patch.description: A cat-burglar dropping from a wall onto a lawn in soft shoes: the balls of both feet meet the turf 28 ms apart (two padded thumps, nothing sharp), the knees give and the heels settle at 110 ms, grass and soil crush under the soles, and the clothes catch up with a last rustle around 150 ms. Outdoors and close: no echo at all.

tracks.note: Left and right foot, 28 ms apart: a drum-skin-like patch of ground hit with something soft. The flam is what makes it two feet and a body.
The weight coming down through the heels as the knees bend: one lower, duller bump at 110 ms.
Grass and soil crushed under the soles: a soft crunch of low, short grains that begins with the first foot.
The turf giving way under the soles: a crumbling, noisy press on something dead and fibrous. It carries the landing on small speakers, where the thumps vanish.
The jacket arriving after the body: a breath of fabric noise, 100 ms long.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A cat to a heavy man with a pack: lower, longer, with more heel.

controls.label: Softness
controls.hint: Bare stone under thin soles to deep moss: the thump loses its edge.

controls.label: Ground
controls.hint: Bare, swept ground to leaves, twigs and gravel.

controls.label: Feet
controls.hint: Both feet together to one after the other.

controls.label: Clothes
controls.hint: Tight, silent gear to a flapping coat.

patch.name: Fast whoosh
patch.description: A thin bamboo cane swung hard past the ear, 180 ms from start to stop: the air tearing along its length (a hiss that sweeps up to 5 kHz at the fastest point, 80 ms in, and back down) and the whistle of the tip itself, a narrow tone that rises and falls with the speed as the air sheds off the rod. Dry, close, no room.

tracks.note: The turbulence along the cane: band noise whose pitch follows the speed of the swing. The body of the whoosh.
The whistle of the tip (the aeolian tone of a thin rod): a tube resonance that sweeps with the speed. It makes the swing thin and fast, not a gust.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: A lazy swing to a whip-fast cut: shorter and higher.

controls.label: Thickness
controls.hint: A whip or a blade, to a staff or a bat: lower and broader.

controls.label: Whistle
controls.hint: Plain rushing air to a singing edge.

patch.name: Heavy whoosh
patch.description: Something the size of a wrecking ball swinging past your head at 18 m/s, closest at 450 ms and a metre away: a low pressure wave you feel before you hear it, the roar of displaced air combing against itself as it passes (the hollow, jet-like sweep), and the pitch of everything sagging as it goes away. Gone by one second.

tracks.note: The displaced air: pink noise through a resonant comb that sweeps (the turbulence interfering with itself), then moved past the listener.
The weight: a fluttering low thrum at 100 to 300 Hz that swells as the object passes. Remove it and the whoosh becomes light.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A swung sandbag to a passing truck: more low thrum, darker air.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: A slow, looming pass to a violent one.

controls.label: Closeness
controls.hint: Passing across the room to grazing your hair.

controls.label: Hollowness
controls.hint: Plain rushing air to a resonant, jet-like sweep.

patch.name: Cave drip
patch.description: Deep in a limestone cave, water gathers on a stalactite and falls two metres into a still pool: three drops (at 0, about 0.75 and 1.5 s, never quite on time), each a clear "plink" whose pitch flicks upward as the bubble closes, with a fainter secondary drip 60 ms after. The cave answers each one with an echo off the far wall 280 ms later and a long dark tail.

tracks.note: The drops: one tuned bubble per event, pitch rising within 30 ms. Each is a slightly different size.
The small droplet thrown up by the first one, landing 60 ms later: higher and much quieter. Without it the drops sound synthetic.
The slap on the water surface: a 5 ms tick of dark noise at each impact, giving the drop a body.

controls.label: Drop size
controls.hint: A fine bead to a fat, heavy drop: lower and rounder.

controls.label: Rate
controls.hint: A slow, patient drip to a quick trickle.

controls.label: Cave size
controls.hint: A wet cellar to a vast cavern: longer tail, later echo.

controls.label: Depth
controls.hint: Beside the pool to far down the tunnel: the echo takes over from the drop.

controls.label: Splash
controls.hint: A clean plink to a messier drop with droplets scattering.

patch.name: Crackling fire (loop)
patch.description: A campfire of dry pine an arm's length away: the soft low flutter of the flames, a steady fine crackle from the embers, sharp resin pops a few times a second with a little wooden knock in each, and now and then a hiss of sap. A 5 s loop; the flames and pops are random, and the end is crossfaded into the start over 0.5 s.

tracks.note: The flames: low noise that flutters irregularly at 8 to 12 times a second, as burning gas does. The warmth and the size of the fire.
The fine crackle: dense tiny pops with very uneven levels. The texture that says "fire" on any speaker.
Resin pockets bursting: sharp ragged pops, a few a second, some much louder than the rest.
The logs themselves cracking: small wooden knocks under some of the pops, so the fire is made of wood.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A candle-sized flame to a roaring bonfire.

controls.label: Crackle
controls.hint: Glowing quietly to spitting and snapping.

controls.label: Distance
controls.hint: Face in the heat to across the camp: the crackle softens, the flutter stays.

controls.label: Wood
controls.hint: Damp, hissing logs to bone-dry kindling: sharper, brighter pops.

patch.name: Rain (loop)
patch.description: Steady rain in a garden, heard from under a porch roof: thousands of small drops ticking on leaves and gravel (the bright patter), fat drops from the gutter plopping into a puddle a few times a second, and the far wash of rain on the whole street behind them. A 6 s stereo loop; nothing in it is periodic, and the end is crossfaded into the start over 0.6 s.

tracks.note: The near drops: separate ticks, each with its own pitch and place. This is what makes it rain and not hiss.
Heavy drops falling from the gutter into standing water: rising-pitch plops, sparse and louder.
All the rain you cannot pick out: a soft band of noise that breathes slowly. It fills the gaps between ticks.

controls.label: Intensity
controls.hint: A light drizzle to a downpour.

controls.label: Drop size
controls.hint: Fine mist to big heavy drops: lower, longer ticks.

controls.label: Puddles
controls.hint: Dry ground to water standing everywhere.

controls.label: Shelter
controls.hint: Out in it, to behind a closed window.

patch.name: Water splash
patch.description: A rock the size of two fists thrown into a pond from the bank, four metres away: the flat slap as it breaks the surface, the deep hollow "gloop" of the air pocket closing behind it at 60 ms (its pitch rising as the cavity shrinks), the hiss of the crown of water going up, and its droplets raining back from 200 to 900 ms, big ones first. Open air, a short reflection from the far bank.

tracks.note: The first 30 ms: the surface breaking. A hard broad noise burst; it tells how flat and how fast the thing hit.
The cavity collapsing under water: a low resonant bubble at 150 to 400 Hz whose pitch climbs. The weight of the splash, in the range small speakers have.
The sheet of water thrown up: a wash of noise that opens and dies over 400 ms.
The water coming back down: drops with rising pitch, the heavy ones first and the fine spray last.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A pebble to a boulder (or a body): deeper gloop, longer rain of drops.

controls.label: Impact
controls.hint: Slipping in edge-first to a flat, stinging belly flop.

controls.label: Spray
controls.hint: A clean plunge to a wide, hissing crown and a shower of droplets.

controls.label: Distance
controls.hint: At your feet to across the lake.

patch.name: Stream (loop)
patch.description: A shallow brook running over stones in a wood, heard from the bank: hundreds of small bubbles a second gurgling between the stones (each a little rising note between 300 Hz and 2 kHz), a deeper, slower glug where the water drops into a hollow, and the soft continuous hiss of the riffle. A 6 s stereo loop; everything is random, and the seam is crossfaded over 0.6 s.

tracks.note: The gurgle: a dense cloud of rising-pitch bubbles spread across the stream. The voice of the water.
The hollow under a small fall: big slow bubbles, 6 to 9 a second, in the 150 to 400 Hz range. Gives the stream depth.
White water over the shallow stones: an airy hiss that shifts slowly, so the bubbles sit in moving water.

controls.label: Flow
controls.hint: A trickle after a dry week to a brook in full spate.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A finger-wide rivulet to a wide, deep stream: lower, rounder bubbles.

controls.label: Pools
controls.hint: Flat shallows to deep hollows that glug.

controls.label: Distance
controls.hint: Feet in the water to somewhere through the trees.

patch.name: Thunder
patch.description: Lightning strikes about 600 m away over open country. The crack arrives first: a tearing, splitting burst of 250 ms. Then the boom of the main channel at 120 ms, and after it the rumble rolls on for five seconds as sound from the farther parts of the bolt arrives, in three or four uneven surges (near 0.9, 1.7 and 2.8 s), each darker than the last, until only a low murmur is left.

tracks.note: The tearing crack of the near part of the bolt: a ragged cluster of sharp pops, not a single click. Only present when the strike is close.
The main body: dark noise that slams in at 120 ms and darkens as it decays. Kept strong from 80 to 300 Hz so it is felt on small speakers.
The rolling rumble: the same thunder from farther along the bolt, arriving in uneven surges and fading over five seconds.

controls.label: Distance
controls.hint: Right overhead (all crack) to a storm beyond the hills (all rumble).

controls.label: Power
controls.hint: A small bolt to one that shakes the windows.

controls.label: Roll
controls.hint: One clap and done, to a rumble that goes on and on.

controls.label: Tear
controls.hint: A single snap to a long ripping crackle before the boom.

patch.name: Wind (loop)
patch.description: Wind over an open hillside with a hut on it: a broad rush of air that swells and falls in gusts every few seconds, a low buffeting underneath when it leans on the walls, and a thin whistle where it gets through a gap in the window frame, rising when the gust does. An 8 s stereo loop; the gusts repeat exactly once per loop (they are tied to 1/8 Hz and its multiples) and the seam is crossfaded over 1 s.

tracks.note: The air itself: pink noise whose colour and level rise and fall together with the gusts (one slow, one twice as fast, both whole cycles per loop).
Pressure on the walls and in the ears: slow, irregular low thumping between 60 and 200 Hz. The weight of the wind.
The gap in the window frame: noise ringing in a narrow tube, its pitch pushed up by each gust. The detail that gives the wind a voice.

controls.label: Strength
controls.hint: A breeze to a gale: brighter, fuller and heavier on the walls.

controls.label: Gusts
controls.hint: An even, steady blow to wild surges and lulls.

controls.label: Whistle
controls.hint: Open country with nothing to whistle through, to a howling gap.

controls.label: Gap
controls.hint: The pitch of the whistle: a wide crack that moans, to a keyhole that shrieks.

patch.name: Bounce
patch.description: A ball bouncing in a 16-bit console game, on its two-operator FM chip. Each bounce is a rubbery boing: the pitch dips from 330 to 150 Hz in 40 ms as the ball squashes and springs back up past 400 Hz, while the FM index flares and relaxes. Three bounces, each sooner and quieter than the last, through the console's slightly grainy converter.

tracks.note: One squash and rebound, repeated as the ball settles.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A beach ball to a marble.

controls.label: Bounces
controls.hint: One boing to a ball that keeps going.

controls.label: Rubber
controls.hint: A dull round ball to a twangy, brassy one.

controls.label: Springiness
controls.hint: A dead ball that stops fast to a lively one with long, even hops.

patch.name: Coin
patch.description: A coin picked up on an 8-bit console with two pulse channels. One 50% square plays B5 for 70 ms and jumps a fourth to E6, which fades for 400 ms through the chip's 16 volume steps. No attack, no vibrato, nothing else: the jump is the reward.

tracks.note: The only channel: a square that steps up once and decays.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A big gold coin to a tiny gem.

controls.label: Jump
controls.hint: How far the second note leaps: a minor third to an octave and a fifth.

controls.label: Length
controls.hint: A quick blip to a long ringing coin.

controls.label: Duty
controls.hint: A thin, nasal 12.5% pulse to a full hollow square.

patch.name: 8-bit explosion
patch.description: Something blows up on an 8-bit console. The noise channel starts at a fast clock (bright hiss) and is stepped down to a slow one over 700 ms, so the roar sinks into a rattling grumble, while its volume falls through all 16 levels, 50 ms each. The triangle channel adds the only bass the machine has: a rumble sliding from 120 to 50 Hz that jitters at random.

tracks.note: The blast: clocked noise whose clock slows, with a staircase fade.
The weight: a stepped triangle sliding down and shaking.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A popped crate to a boss going up: longer and deeper.

controls.label: Rumble
controls.hint: Noise alone to a blast with a shaking bass under it.

controls.label: Grumble
controls.hint: A smooth hiss that just fades to one that breaks up into rattling chunks.

controls.label: Crunch
controls.hint: A cleaner 6-bit machine to a brutal 2-bit one.

patch.name: Hurt
patch.description: The player takes a hit on an 8-bit console. The noise channel cracks for 50 ms while a thin 12.5% pulse drops more than an octave in 130 ms, its pitch thrown up and down 45 times a second so it sounds scrambled rather than sung. Cut dead at 140 ms. Harsh and short, as damage should be.

tracks.note: The pain: a falling pulse with a violent square wobble.
The impact: the noise channel at a low clock rate, so it is gritty, not hissy.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A big boss grunt to a small critter squeal.

controls.label: Shake
controls.hint: A plain falling tone to a scrambled, glitching one.

controls.label: Crack
controls.hint: Only the yelp to a hard noisy smack on the front.

controls.label: Length
controls.hint: A quick flinch to a long, sinking defeat.

patch.name: Jump
patch.description: A character jumping on an 8-bit console. A 25% pulse sweeps up an octave and a half in 190 ms, its volume stepping down as it goes, and the noise channel spits a 25 ms scuff at take-off for the feet leaving the ground. It is cut off, not faded: the channel is needed for the next sound.

tracks.note: The jump: pitch is height.
Take-off: one short burst from the noise channel.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A heavy hero to a tiny, springy one.

controls.label: Height
controls.hint: A small hop to a huge leap: how far the pitch climbs.

controls.label: Duty
controls.hint: A thin, nasal 12.5% pulse to a full hollow square.

controls.label: Feet
controls.hint: A clean synthetic jump to one that kicks off the ground.

patch.name: Laser
patch.description: A shot from a home-computer sound chip with a real filter. A pulse falls from 2.1 kHz to 260 Hz in 140 ms while its width opens from a thin sliver to a square, and the chip's resonant low-pass closes behind it. The player routine retriggers it twice more, quieter each time, 70 ms apart: the cheap echo of the era. Low sample rate leaves metallic aliasing on top.

tracks.note: The shot and its two software echoes.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A heavy cannon to a small pea-shooter.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: A long descending beam to a quick pew.

controls.label: Echo
controls.hint: A single dry shot to three that trail off down a corridor.

controls.label: Squelch
controls.hint: A plain pulse to a wet, whistling filter sweep.

controls.label: Grit
controls.hint: A clean chip to a cheap one that rings and aliases.

patch.name: Menu select
patch.description: The cursor moving in an 8-bit menu, played on the triangle channel, which has no volume control: it is either on or off. A 16-step triangle at 660 Hz for 35 ms, then an octave up for 45 ms, switched off dead. The staircase of the 4-bit wave gives it a faint buzzing edge that a clean triangle does not have.

tracks.note: One channel, two pitches, no envelope.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: Move it per menu row, or drop it for a back sound.

controls.label: Leap
controls.hint: A flat double blip to a jump of an octave and a fifth.

controls.label: Length
controls.hint: A tick to two clear notes.

controls.label: Steps
controls.hint: A buzzing 4-level staircase to a smooth, flute-like triangle.

patch.name: 1-up
patch.description: An extra life on an 8-bit console: a six-note rising figure on the first pulse channel, 80 ms a note, each note re-struck by a volume ramp, the last one held and faded. The second pulse channel plays the same line 80 ms late with a thinner duty and less volume, the trick old games used for echo when they had no reverb.

tracks.note: The tune.
The same tune one note late on the other channel: a fake echo.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: Transpose the jingle to your game's key.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: A stately fanfare to a quick sparkle.

controls.label: Echo
controls.hint: One dry channel to a full two-channel echo.

controls.label: Pluck
controls.hint: Smooth organ-like notes to sharply struck ones.

controls.label: Duty
controls.hint: A thin, nasal lead to a full hollow square.

patch.name: Power-up
patch.description: A power-up taken on an 8-bit console. One pulse channel cannot play chords, so it runs a major arpeggio at three notes every tenth of a second and walks it up the scale: six climbing triads in 630 ms, the last one held with a fast square vibrato. The triangle channel doubles the root of each triad two octaves down as a bass.

tracks.note: The arpeggio: fast enough to blur into rising chords.
The triangle channel: fixed volume, the root of each triad.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A weighty armour upgrade to a tiny speed boost.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: A slow, grand fanfare to a quick zip upward.

controls.label: Duty
controls.hint: A thin, nasal 12.5% pulse to a full hollow square.

controls.label: Bass
controls.hint: The arpeggio alone to a full two-channel fanfare.

controls.label: Wobble
controls.hint: A steady last note to a wide, warbling one.

patch.name: Computer data chirps
patch.description: A starship console working something out, heard through its small panel speaker. Eleven short bursts of data in about a second, uneven like a teletype: each is a slice of an integer bytebeat formula at a different pitch, so they are little broken melodies rather than beeps. Between them a relay ticks. At 1.15 s the answer arrives: two clean notes, up a fourth.
