tracks.note: The thinking: bytebeat slices. Every event has its own randomness, pitch and length.
Hardware behind the panel: gives the bursts a machine to live in.
The result: the only clean, pitched thing, so it reads as 'done'.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: A slow, pondering mainframe to a frantic burst of traffic.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A big old low-voiced machine to a tiny chirpy droid.

controls.label: Corruption
controls.hint: Tidy patterns to skipping, stuttering, bit-flipped garbage.

controls.label: Answer
controls.hint: No result tone at all, or a clear two-note 'done'.

controls.label: Panel speaker
controls.hint: Clean and direct to a cheap buzzing speaker in a metal box.

patch.name: Force field hum (loop)
patch.description: Standing a metre from a containment field across a doorway, a 4 s seamless loop. The field's emitters hum at 58 Hz with a hollow, mostly odd set of harmonics, slowly breathing through a phaser as the field ripples. Its metal frame sings faintly along. Somewhere inside, an unstable current wanders and flips (a quiet buzzing that never repeats), and every so often dust touches the field and pops.

tracks.note: The hum: weight at 58 to 290 Hz so it survives small speakers. The phaser runs exactly two cycles per loop.
The unstable current: a Lorenz attractor flipping between two lobes. This is what makes it dangerous instead of a fridge.
Dust and moths meeting the field: sparse pops with ragged tails.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A deep generator drone to a higher, tenser hum.

controls.label: Instability
controls.hint: A healthy steady field to one that buzzes and spits, about to fail.

controls.label: Edge
controls.hint: Soft and dull behind glass to bright, buzzing and close.

controls.label: Ripple
controls.hint: How deeply the field breathes.

patch.name: Blaster bolt
patch.description: A heavy plasma blaster fired down a ship's corridor. 0 ms: the capacitor snaps, a 15 ms digital crack. 2 ms: the bolt leaves, an FM tone whose pitch and sidebands collapse together (a 'bwow' from 1.9 kHz to 150 Hz in 220 ms), slightly overheated. 15 to 200 ms: sparks spit off the muzzle, each a tiny falling chirp. The steel corridor answers with a short ringing slap.

tracks.note: The capacitor letting go: the first 15 ms, stepped digital noise so it reads as electric, not as gunpowder.
The bolt itself. The carrier falls while the modulator's ratio falls faster, so the timbre growls downward instead of just dropping in pitch.
Sparks off the muzzle after the shot: separate little chirps, not hiss.

controls.label: Caliber
controls.hint: Small sidearm pew to a heavy, low cannon bolt.

controls.label: Length
controls.hint: A quick stab to a long drawn-out bwooow.

controls.label: Heat
controls.hint: A clean beam to an overdriven, spitting one with more sparks.

controls.label: Corridor
controls.hint: Dry and close, or ringing down a long metal passage.

patch.name: Plasma charge-up
patch.description: A plasma cannon's coil charging for 1.6 s before it is ready to fire. Two unstable oscillators feed each other inside the coil: at first a low warm buzz, then as the charge builds they rise two octaves and begin to tear. A containment pulse throbs under it, slow at first and blurring into a buzz at the top. A thin capacitor whine climbs above everything. At 1.6 s the charge locks with a small relay tick and the coil rings out for a moment in the housing.

tracks.note: The charge itself: cross-modulated sines that climb and lose stability. The tremolo is the containment pulse speeding up.
Capacitor whine: the thin tone that tells you how full it is.
The relay that says ready, right as the rise ends.

controls.label: Charge time
controls.hint: A half-second snap charge to a three-second build.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A pistol cell to a ship's main gun: lower and heavier.

controls.label: Instability
controls.hint: A clean, controlled hum to a charge that tears and screams near the top.

controls.label: Pulse
controls.hint: How hard the containment field throbs.

controls.label: Whine
controls.hint: The thin rising capacitor tone: none to piercing.

patch.name: Power down
patch.description: The main breaker is pulled on a ship's deck and everything on it dies. 0 ms: the breaker handle, a heavy plastic-and-steel clack. From 60 ms the turbine generator, with nothing left to drive it, winds down like a stopping tape over 1.8 s: its whine and the hum of the lights fall together, slowing as they go, into a growl and then nothing. At 1.5 s a last relay drops out somewhere in the dark.

tracks.note: The cause: a hand pulling the handle. Short and dry, in front of everything.
The machine. It plays steadily; the varispeed is what stops it, so pitch and time slow together the way a real rotor does.
Mains hum of the lighting: the low body under the whine, dying on the same curve.
One last relay letting go: the full stop.

controls.label: Wind-down
controls.hint: A light that just cuts out to a huge rotor taking seconds to stop.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A desk gadget to a reactor hall: lower and heavier.

controls.label: Whine
controls.hint: Mostly low hum, or a screaming turbine on top.

controls.label: Switch
controls.hint: How loud the breaker and the last relay are.

controls.label: Deck
controls.hint: Dry and close to a ringing metal hall.

patch.name: Power up
patch.description: An old bridge console is switched on. 0 ms: a contactor slams in (steel on steel). 20 ms: the degauss coil shudders, a 100 Hz buzz that shakes hard and dies away over 600 ms. From 80 ms the cooling fan spins up from standstill to speed, straining at first. From 500 ms the logic comes alive: a stutter of start-up self-test glitches that clears as it stabilises. At 1.35 s the system is up and says so with a soft, slightly detuned open fifth that fades into the fan noise.

tracks.note: Mains thrown in: hard, metallic, the first thing you hear.
The coil shudder old tubes make at switch-on: a buzzing 100 Hz saw that wobbles in level and dies. This is the weight.
The fan getting up to speed: load is high while it accelerates, then it settles.
Logic waking: corrupted bytebeat that gets cleaner (chaos falls) as the system finds its feet.
Up and running: a calm fifth, each partial doubled a few cents apart so it glows instead of beeping.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A handheld waking up to a whole engine room coming on line.

controls.label: Shudder
controls.hint: The coil buzz at switch-on: a faint hum to a cabinet-shaking thump.

controls.label: Fan
controls.hint: Silent solid-state gear to a loud whirring cooling fan.

controls.label: Self-test
controls.hint: A clean start to a long stutter of boot garbage.

controls.label: Ready tone
controls.hint: No chime, or a clear glowing 'online'.

patch.name: Scanner sweep
patch.description: A hand-held sensor passed slowly over a wall and back, 1.5 s. The scanner's beam is heard as air ringing in a narrow tube whose length changes with the sweep: the hollow tone glides from 320 Hz up to 1.9 kHz at 750 ms and back down, fluttering 21 times a second like scan lines. At the top of the sweep, when the beam crosses something, it pings (a small glassy FM note) and the ping echoes twice inside the device.

tracks.note: The sweep: noise ringing in a tube resonator whose pitch follows the hand. Odd harmonics make it hollow, which reads as a beam rather than a synth.
The find: lands where the sweep turns round. The delay is the device's own little echo.

controls.label: Sweep speed
controls.hint: A slow careful pass to a quick flick.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A big deep-scan unit to a small shrill one.

controls.label: Scan lines
controls.hint: A smooth beam to a hard, buzzing flicker.

controls.label: Focus
controls.hint: A breathy wide beam to a tight whistling one.

controls.label: Ping
controls.hint: Nothing found, or a clear echoing contact.

patch.name: Energy shield impact
patch.description: A shot stops against a personal energy shield. The field behaves like a huge thin glass bowl: at 0 ms it is struck and rings with a wobbling, beating hum (two detuned sets of modes), but a ring modulator turns that ring electric and wrong. 0 to 250 ms: the surface crackles where it was hit as the charge spreads. A soft low 'bwom' is the field flexing inward and recovering over 300 ms.

tracks.note: The shield as an object: a glass bowl 2 m wide, its modes beating. The ring modulator keeps some of the bowl and adds inharmonic sidebands, so it is glassy but not glass.
The field bowing in and springing back: the weight of the hit. A buzzing low tone, not a clean sine.
The charge spreading across the surface from the point of impact.

controls.label: Shield size
controls.hint: A wrist buckler to a ship's deflector: lower, longer ring.

controls.label: Hit force
controls.hint: A glancing pebble to a cannon round: harder, brighter, with more flex.

controls.label: Charge
controls.hint: Nearly plain glass to a fully electric, alien clang.

controls.label: Wobble
controls.hint: A steady ring to a fast shimmering flutter.

controls.label: Crackle
controls.hint: Surface discharge: none to a shower.

patch.name: Teleport out
patch.description: Someone is beamed away from a quiet room. 0 to 900 ms: the body dissolves into a column of glittering grains of tone that thicken and climb from 700 Hz to 9 kHz. Under them a hollow chord of the transporter beam swells and swirls. At 950 ms the column is gone and the air it left behind claps shut: a soft dull pop, and the room rings for a moment.

tracks.note: The body coming apart: hundreds of small tonal grains whose range climbs. Density builds, then thins as there is nothing left.
The carrier beam: a hollow, odd-harmonic chord that opens up and is swirled by a phaser.
Air rushing into the space the body left: a dull, pitchless pop. Without it the sound has no ending.

controls.label: Beam time
controls.hint: A quick blink away to a slow, ceremonial dissolve.

controls.label: Glitter
controls.hint: A few sparse motes to a dense sparkling column.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A deep cargo transporter to a small, high personal one.

controls.label: Swirl
controls.hint: A steady beam to a fast, bubbling vortex.

controls.label: Pop
controls.hint: How hard the air claps shut at the end.

patch.name: Warp jump
patch.description: A starship jumps to light speed, heard from just behind it. 0 to 1.2 s: space is pulled in: the ring of a huge struck hull plate played backwards in a cathedral-sized reverb, swelling out of nothing, while the drive's chord is stretched upward two octaves through a jet-like flanger. 1.2 s: the jump, a slammed low boom with a cracking front edge. After it the ship is already gone: its wake tears away past you (noise with real Doppler at 140 m/s) and the boom rolls off into empty space for three seconds.

tracks.note: The suck-in: a metal plate hit, drowned in reverb, then reversed so it climaxes exactly at the jump (the reversed sound is 1.2 s long).
The drive spooling: a stacked saw chord dragged up two octaves, faster and faster. The flanger's delay closes to almost nothing, like a jet passing.
The moment: a huge soft-struck membrane for the boom (weight at 60 to 200 Hz), a 30 ms noise crack on its front, pushed into a tube for harmonics small speakers can play.
The ship leaving: the doppler puts the closest pass at the jump, so only the falling, receding half is heard.

controls.label: Power
controls.hint: A small courier's hop to a capital ship tearing a hole.

controls.label: Pull
controls.hint: How strongly space is sucked in before the jump.

controls.label: Wake
controls.hint: A clean vanish, or a long tearing whoosh as it leaves.

controls.label: Void
controls.hint: A dry thump to a boom rolling away through an enormous space.

patch.name: Cancel / back
patch.description: Never mind: two tines of a wooden thumb piano plucked with the flesh of the thumb, stepping down a minor third 75 ms apart, each damped by the hand so it does not sing. The thumb lands on the board with a small woody knock. Dry and unhurried; a step back, not a failure.

tracks.note: The two notes going down. Muted so they read as a gesture, not a melody.
The thumb landing on the wooden box: the material of the set.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: Move the pair up or down to sit under your confirm sound.

controls.label: Drop
controls.hint: How far the second note falls: a small step to a fifth.

controls.label: Mute
controls.hint: Open ringing tines to a short choked thunk.

controls.label: Wood
controls.hint: How much of the wooden box knocks under the notes.

patch.name: Error buzz
patch.description: Not allowed: a small piezo buzzer in a plastic case sounds twice, 90 ms each with a 50 ms gap. Two rough FM tones a flattened fifth apart beat against each other so it reads as no without being loud, and the case gives it a boxy 1.1 kHz honk. Flat, short, stops dead.

tracks.note: Two self-modulating carriers a tritone apart: the buzz and its disagreement.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A low refusal to a higher, lighter nope.

controls.label: Harshness
controls.hint: A dull hum to a rasping buzzer.

controls.label: Clash
controls.hint: One plain tone to two that grind against each other.

controls.label: Length
controls.hint: Two quick blips to two longer buzzes that almost join.

patch.name: Hover tick
patch.description: A pointer passing over an item: a fingernail barely touching the rim of a thin glass. One tiny note near 2.6 kHz with a breath of two glass overtones, a soft 1.5 ms front so it never clicks, gone in 40 ms. Meant to be played quietly and often.

tracks.note: The whole sound: three glass partials whose upper two die almost at once.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: Step it up or down per item for a row that plays a scale.

controls.label: Length
controls.hint: A dry tick to a small ringing ping.

controls.label: Glass
controls.hint: A plain soft blip to a brighter, glassier touch.

controls.label: Softness
controls.hint: A crisp nail tap to a rounded, clickless fade-in.

patch.name: Mechanical click
patch.description: One key of a mechanical keyboard pressed home. The plastic stem snaps past the click leaf (a sharp 3 kHz tick at 0 ms), bottoms out on the plate 11 ms later (a lower, boxier knock around 520 Hz) and the coil spring under it answers with a faint high ping for 100 ms. Close, dry, on a desk.

tracks.note: The click leaf: the first 3 ms, bright and thin. This is what makes it mechanical.
The stem hitting the plate: the weight of the key, a few ms after the snap.
The coil spring ringing after the hit: quiet, but it is the tail that says metal inside plastic.

controls.label: Travel
controls.hint: A short laptop key to a deep, slow switch: the gap between the snap and the bottom.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A light keycap to a heavy one on a thick plate.

controls.label: Snap
controls.hint: A quiet linear switch to a loud clicky one.

controls.label: Spring
controls.hint: How much the spring pings after the key lands.

patch.name: Notification chime
patch.description: Something arrived: three small FM bells stacked in fifths, 110 ms apart, each struck bright and mellowing within a quarter second while it rings on for a second. A single quiet echo and a studio plate put it a little way off, so it asks for attention without startling.

tracks.note: The three notes: a strike whose overtones fade faster than the tone.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A deep door chime to a small phone ping.

controls.label: Pace
controls.hint: A quick flick of three notes to a slow, calm arpeggio.

controls.label: Brightness
controls.hint: Soft and round to a hard, glittering strike.

controls.label: Ring
controls.hint: Short dry notes to long ringing ones.

controls.label: Space
controls.hint: Right at the screen to across a quiet room.

patch.name: Panel close
patch.description: A panel sliding shut like a drawer on felt runners: an FM tone falls a fifth and loses its overtones over 160 ms, and at 165 ms the panel lands with a soft, padded thud near 170 Hz. The landing is what tells it apart from Panel open: this one arrives somewhere.

tracks.note: The panel moving: brightness and pitch falling together.
The stop: a padded box thud. Gives the sound an end and some weight.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A small tooltip to a full-screen sheet: lower, slower, heavier landing.

controls.label: Brightness
controls.hint: A dull hum to a reedy, buzzing slide.

controls.label: Thud
controls.hint: A panel that just fades out to one that lands firmly.

controls.label: Padding
controls.hint: Felt-lined and dead to a bare wooden knock.

patch.name: Panel open
patch.description: A panel unfolding into view: a soft synthetic tone that climbs a fifth and opens from dull to clear over 200 ms, pushing a breath of air outward ahead of it, then settles in a small room. Gentle and rounded; nothing lands.

tracks.note: The panel: harmonics that are let in as it opens, on a rising pitch.
Displaced air, rising with the tone: the size of the thing that moved.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A small tooltip to a full-screen sheet: lower and slower.

controls.label: Brightness
controls.hint: Muffled and felt-like to open and reedy.

controls.label: Rise
controls.hint: Almost level to a clear upward leap.

controls.label: Air
controls.hint: A pure tone to mostly a breath of air.

controls.label: Space
controls.hint: Flat on the glass to a panel in a room.

patch.name: Slider detent
patch.description: One notch of a dial with a ceramic detent wheel: a hard, dry 2.3 kHz tick as the ball drops into the groove, with a tiny low bump of the knob in the fingers, over in 20 ms. Drive Position from the slider value and a drag plays a rising row of ticks.

tracks.note: The detent itself: a few ceramic modes, heavily damped.
The knob settling in the hand: two cycles of a low bump, felt more than heard.

controls.label: Position
controls.hint: Where on the slider: low end to high end, a little over an octave of ticks.

controls.label: Hardness
controls.hint: A rubbery soft stop to steel on ceramic.

controls.label: Ring
controls.hint: A dead tick to a small ringing tink.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A weightless tick to a knob with some mass behind it.

patch.name: Soft click
patch.description: A fingertip pressing a soft silicone button, heard from typing distance. The pad of the finger lands (a 2 ms dull pat of air), the rubber dome gives with a rounded, pitchless knock around 430 Hz, and it is over in 50 ms. Dry and close; the default tap for anything pressed hundreds of times.

tracks.note: The body: a small plastic skin giving way. Sets the size of the key.
Skin on the surface: 15 ms of dull air that makes it a finger and not a beep.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A wide space bar to a tiny keypad dot.

controls.label: Touch
controls.hint: A soft fingertip to a fingernail: more edge on the front.

controls.label: Body
controls.hint: Dead and damped to a hollow little knock.

controls.label: Skin
controls.hint: How much of the finger you hear on top of the key.

patch.name: Soft confirm
patch.description: A friendly yes: two small glass tumblers tapped with a felt stick, the second a fourth above the first and 85 ms later, answering it. Each has the uneven partials of real glass and a slow shimmer; the felt gives a short warm bump under each note. A small bright room keeps them from sounding like a test tone.

tracks.note: The two glasses; the second note is the answer.
The felt stick: a short octave-below bump that gives the notes weight on small speakers.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: Higher is lighter and more toy-like; lower is calmer.

controls.label: Length
controls.hint: Two quick taps to a lingering chime.

controls.label: Shimmer
controls.hint: Plain glass to a slow, beating sparkle in a bigger room.

controls.label: Warmth
controls.hint: Thin and glassy to round and padded.

patch.name: Success flourish
patch.description: Done, and done well: a quick upward run over four bright harp strings (a major chord to the octave, 55 ms apart), the top note left ringing, and from 150 ms a sprinkle of glass dust that thins and climbs as it falls away. A studio plate holds it together. About a second and a half; for the end of a task, not every click.

tracks.note: The gesture: four plucked strings going up, each a little louder.
The reward: tiny glass pings after the run, rising and thinning.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A warm low strum to a bright music-box run.

controls.label: Sparkle
controls.hint: Just the harp to a shower of glass dust after it.

controls.label: Strings
controls.hint: Soft gut strings to hard bright wire.

controls.label: Ring
controls.hint: A short dry run to strings that sing on.

controls.label: Space
controls.hint: Dry and close to a wide, glowing plate.

patch.name: Swipe
patch.description: A card flicked sideways across a touchscreen: 180 ms of air that swells and rises in pitch as the finger accelerates, with a faint hollow whistle from the gap under the card. No click at either end; it starts from nothing and thins out.

tracks.note: The movement: a band of noise sweeping with the gesture.
A hollow pitch inside the air, so the direction is heard and not only felt.

controls.label: Direction
controls.hint: Rising for forward or open, falling for back or dismiss.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: A slow drag to a quick flick.

controls.label: Brightness
controls.hint: A heavy sheet moving to a thin, airy flick.

controls.label: Whistle
controls.hint: Plain air to a clear hollow pitch in it.

patch.name: Text blip
patch.description: One syllable of a small character talking, for dialogue that types itself out: a 55 ms voiced "eh" from a tiny throat, its pitch dipping a little as it stops. Trigger one per letter with variations and the Pitch and Vowel controls wander into babble.

tracks.note: The whole sound: a throat, not a beep, so each character can have a voice.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A low grumble to a high chirpy speaker.

controls.label: Vowel
controls.hint: ah, eh, ee, oh, oo: vary it per letter for babble.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A mouse to an ogre: the throat, not the pitch.

controls.label: Length
controls.hint: A clipped tick of a voice to a full syllable.

controls.label: Robot
controls.hint: A soft living voice to a pressed, whistling machine.

patch.name: Toggle off
patch.description: The same rocker switch thrown off. The latch lands duller, as a short puff of dark air, and with it a damped string-like tone sags a fourth over 70 ms as the light behind the switch dies. Lower, shorter and rounder than Toggle on.

tracks.note: The state going out: a muted pluck whose pitch falls.
The switch landing: darker than the on tick, more thud than click.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A big panel switch to a tiny checkbox.

controls.label: Fall
controls.hint: How far the tone drops: a nudge to a full octave slump.

controls.label: Click
controls.hint: All tone to mostly the dull switch.

controls.label: Length
controls.hint: A choked blip to a tone that rings a little.

patch.name: Toggle on
patch.description: A small rocker switch thrown on. The plastic latch ticks over at 0 ms, and 8 ms later a soft indicator tone slides up a fifth in 55 ms and fades, like a light coming up behind the switch. Pairs with Toggle off.

tracks.note: The physical switch: a dry plastic tick that says something moved.
The state: a tone that rises, so it reads as on without looking.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A big panel switch to a tiny checkbox.

controls.label: Rise
controls.hint: How far the tone climbs: a nudge to a bright leap of an octave.

controls.label: Click
controls.hint: All tone to mostly the plastic switch.

controls.label: Length
controls.hint: A clipped blip to a tone that lingers.

patch.name: Warning ping
patch.description: Look here: the rim of a small glass bowl tapped twice with a fingernail, 170 ms apart, the same note both times and the second softer. The bowl is not quite round, so its modes beat slowly, and a tiled room rings briefly behind it. Insistent because it repeats, not because it is harsh.

tracks.note: The note: rim modes of a glass bowl, a little imperfect.
The fingernail: 3 ms of bright contact so both taps are counted clearly.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A larger bowl for a calm caution, a small one for a sharp ping.

controls.label: Urgency
controls.hint: Two patient taps to a fast, even double knock.

controls.label: Ring
controls.hint: A damped tink to a bowl left to sing.

controls.label: Hardness
controls.hint: A fingertip to a metal spoon.

controls.label: Wobble
controls.hint: A perfect bowl to one whose ring beats and wavers.

patch.name: Car passing by
patch.description: A family hatchback passing on a two-lane road at 70 km/h, heard from the pavement six metres from its path: the engine note climbs out of the distance, a four-cylinder at 2800 rpm, the tyres hiss on the asphalt louder than the engine as it draws level at 1.9 s, the whole sound drops a tone as it passes, and the exhaust is what you hear last. Left to right, stereo, four seconds.

tracks.note: The four-cylinder under light load, holding its speed. Its firing pulses are what the Doppler shift is heard on.
Rubber on asphalt: a broad hiss around 1 kHz, the loudest thing when the car is close.
The air the car pushes aside: a low buffeting rush that gives the pass its body.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: Rolling through a car park to flat out on a motorway: a quicker, deeper drop in pitch, higher revs, more tyre.

controls.label: Closeness
controls.hint: A road across the field to standing on the kerb.

controls.label: Engine
controls.hint: A small city car, to a van, to a truck: bigger, lower, louder against the tyres.

controls.label: Wet road
controls.hint: Dry asphalt to a road running with water: a bright, spraying hiss.

patch.name: Engine idling (loop)
patch.description: An older four-cylinder petrol car idling at the kerb, bonnet shut, heard from beside the front wheel: 780 rpm, 26 firings a second with one cylinder a little weak so it lopes, the valve gear ticking lightly on top, and the exhaust burbling at the back. A 2 s loop that holds exactly 13 engine cycles (two turns each), crossfaded over 150 ms on a cycle boundary.

tracks.note: The firing pulses through the exhaust: the engine itself. Roughness is what makes it an old car and not a test tone.
Tappets: a light metallic tick at twice the firing rate (52 a second), slightly uneven. The mechanical top end you hear standing next to it.
Exhaust gas pulsing out of the tailpipe: low noise chopped at the firing rate, so the idle has breath as well as tone.

controls.label: Idle speed
controls.hint: A slow, lumpy tick-over to a fast, cold-start idle. (Away from the middle the loop relies on its crossfade.)

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A scooter-sized engine to a lorry diesel: lower pipe, heavier pulses.

controls.label: Wear
controls.hint: Fresh from the factory to a tired engine that misses and lopes.

controls.label: Tappets
controls.hint: Bonnet shut and quiet, to a noisy, ticking top end.

controls.label: Exhaust
controls.hint: A whisper-quiet silencer to an open, burbling pipe.

patch.name: Helicopter (loop)
patch.description: A light two-blade helicopter in a hover 150 m away: the main rotor slapping ten times a second (300 rpm), the tail rotor buzzing at 80 Hz, the turbine whining above both, and the downwash hissing in time with the blades. A 2 s stereo loop holding exactly 20 blade slaps, crossfaded over 200 ms.

tracks.note: The main rotor: two blades at 300 rpm, a slap every 100 ms. The "wop-wop" that is the whole character.
The tail rotor: four small blades at 1200 rpm, an 80 Hz buzz with a hard edge. Heard most from the side.
The engine: a steady jet whine and hiss above the rotors. What separates a helicopter from a big fan.
Downwash: air noise that pulses with each blade passing, the soft part of the slap.

controls.label: Distance
controls.hint: Standing under the disc to a speck on the horizon: only the thump of the blades carries.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A two-seat trainer to a heavy-lift transport: slower, deeper blades.

controls.label: Strain
controls.hint: Idling on the pad to hauling a load in a hard turn: louder, harsher slaps.

controls.label: Turbine
controls.hint: How much jet whine sits over the rotors.

patch.name: Jet fly-by
patch.description: A fighter jet crossing low over an airfield at 120 m/s, 250 m up: almost nothing until it is on you, the compressor whine arriving first and thin, then at 1.9 s the pass, and behind it the real sound: the tearing, crackling roar of the exhaust that drops in pitch and takes four seconds to roll away, hollowed by its reflection off the runway. Left to right, stereo, six and a half seconds.

tracks.note: The compressor: a thin whistle you hear from the front, fading as the jet shows its tail.
The exhaust: broadband roar that is quiet in front of the jet and enormous behind it, with the comb of the ground reflection sweeping as the angle changes.
The low end of the exhaust: a rumble from 80 to 250 Hz that arrives with the pass and outlasts everything.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: An airliner on approach to a fast, hard military pass: the onset gets more sudden.

controls.label: Height
controls.hint: Skimming the runway to high overhead: a slower, gentler swell.

controls.label: Afterburner
controls.hint: Throttled back and whistling, to full reheat: crackle, distortion and low thunder.

controls.label: Whine
controls.hint: How much compressor whistle leads the roar.

controls.label: Ground
controls.hint: Open sky to a hard runway under it: the hollow sweep in the roar.

patch.name: Motorbike rev
patch.description: A rider on a big V-twin at a red light, blipping the throttle: off the idle (1100 rpm) a first short blip to 4500 at 250 ms, back down, then a longer, harder one to 6800 at 1.0 s that hangs for a moment before the revs fall, pop and burble on the overrun and settle back into the lumpy idle by 2.3 s. Open pipes, a street with buildings on both sides.

tracks.note: The twin: two cylinders firing unevenly, revs and load drawn by hand so the throttle leads and the engine follows.
Unburnt fuel popping in the pipes as the throttle shuts: a scatter of sharp cracks from 1.25 to 1.9 s.
The carburettors gulping air on each twist of the throttle: a short rising rush under each blip.

controls.label: Revs
controls.hint: A gentle twist of the wrist to bouncing it off the limiter.

controls.label: Bike
controls.hint: A buzzing 125, a mid-size twin, to a big slow cruiser.

controls.label: Pipes
controls.hint: A legal, muffled silencer to straight-through open pipes.

controls.label: Pops
controls.hint: A clean engine to one that bangs and crackles when the throttle closes.

controls.label: Wear
controls.hint: A tight, even engine to a loose old one.

patch.name: Bow shot
patch.description: A longbow loosed beside your ear in a wood. 0 ms: the fingers let go and the string snaps forward, a short dull twang at 82 Hz, slapped silent against the bracer within 150 ms (a real waveguide string, muted fast). 3 ms: the limbs kick, a wooden knock in the bow's body. 10 ms on: the arrow leaves, a thin hiss with fletching flutter that drops in pitch as it flies away at 55 m/s. The trees give back a soft scatter.

tracks.note: The bowstring: plucked close to its middle with soft fingers, a little stiff, and choked by the mute curve the way a bracer stops it.
The bow stave kicking in the hand: a small hollow wooden box. This is the 'thock' that makes it a bow and not a guitar.
The arrow in flight: a narrow hiss, fluttered by the fletching (fast tremolo), carried away by the doppler so it falls in pitch and fades.

controls.label: Draw weight
controls.hint: A light hunting bow to a heavy war bow: deeper twang, harder kick, faster arrow.

controls.label: Twang
controls.hint: A well-silenced thump to a long buzzing string.

controls.label: Arrow
controls.hint: Just the bow, or a loud hissing shaft leaving it.

controls.label: Fletching
controls.hint: A smooth bolt to big fluttering feathers.

patch.name: Bullet fly-by
patch.description: You are being shot at across open ground and the round misses your head by a metre. The bullet is heard before the gun: 0 to 150 ms it comes in as a rising, buzzing whizz (the slug's spin modulating the air it tears, a harsh tone inside a hiss), passing at 150 ms with a tiny sharp crack as its shock wave slaps your ear, and is gone in another 150 ms, its pitch dropped almost an octave. About 650 ms later the rifle's own report finally arrives from 200 m away: a dull, low thump with all its top end eaten by the air, and a short roll off the ground.

tracks.note: The round in the air: a chaotic buzz (a logistic map on the edge of a tone) is the spinning slug. Steady by itself; the doppler does all the motion, pitch and pan.
Torn air around the slug: plain hiss on the same path, so the whizz is not just a tone.
The shock wave at the moment of passing: 6 ms, bright, dry. This is what makes people duck.
The gun, late and far: a soft-struck drum skin through heavy air absorption and a wide outdoor slap. Low and round on purpose.

controls.label: Closeness
controls.hint: Passing ten metres off, a soft zip, to parting your hair: sudden and vicious.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: A lazy spent round to a supersonic rifle bullet: a bigger, quicker pitch drop.

controls.label: Buzz
controls.hint: A clean hiss of air to an angry, hornet-like tumbling slug.

controls.label: Shooter range
controls.hint: Fired from close by, loud and soon, or from far off: later, duller, quieter.

patch.name: Reload
patch.description: A pistol reloaded in a quiet room, close to the microphone. 0 ms: a fresh magazine is slapped into the grip, a steel box seating in a polymer frame with a palm thump behind it. 260 to 400 ms: the slide is racked back, steel dragged over steel for 140 ms, its ridges slowing as the spring loads. 410 ms: let go, the slide slams home (the hardest, brightest hit) and its recoil spring twangs for a moment inside the frame.

tracks.note: Mag seating: a small steel box hit inside the grip. Dented and damped, because it is full of rounds and held in a hand.
The palm and the polymer frame taking the slap: the low part of the click, 2 ms late.
The slide pulled back: a scrape with fairly regular ridges (machined rails), slowing. Quieter than the hits either side of it.
Slide home: steel on steel, a bar this time so it has a pitch different from the magazine. The loudest moment.
The recoil spring ringing after the slam: a very stiff string, choked quickly. Small, but it is the detail that says 'mechanism'.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A pocket pistol's ticks to a heavy rifle's clunks.

controls.label: Hands
controls.hint: A slow, deliberate reload to a fast practised one.

controls.label: Snap
controls.hint: Oiled and soft to dry, hard and clacking.

controls.label: Spring
controls.hint: A tight new gun, or a loose one that twangs and rattles.

controls.label: Room
controls.hint: Dead close-up foley to a bare concrete room.

patch.name: Ricochet
patch.description: A rifle bullet glances off a steel girder in a canyon and whines away. 0 ms: the strike, a hard bright tick on thick steel, and a puff of grit. 5 ms: the deformed slug tumbles off, and its spin sings: a wiry tone that starts at 3.6 kHz and slides down to 900 Hz over 700 ms, wobbling faster and faster as the tumble speeds up, flying away from you so it also dulls and fades. A single canyon echo repeats the whine, darker.

tracks.note: Lead on steel: tiny object, huge force. A small damped bar, struck as hard as possible.
The tumbling slug: a stiff bowed wire, not an oscillator, so the tone is ragged and has rushing air in it. The pitch falls; the wobble (the tumble) speeds up from 9 to 30 Hz.
Paint, rust and lead dust knocked off: a short burst of dry ticks. Places the hit on a real surface.

controls.label: Calibre
controls.hint: A small fast round's thin zing to a heavy slug's low moan.

controls.label: Whine length
controls.hint: A quick 'pting' to a long cartoon-western peeeoww.

controls.label: Tumble
controls.hint: A clean spinning zing to a wildly wobbling, deformed slug.

controls.label: Surface
controls.hint: What it hit.

controls.label: Canyon
controls.hint: No echo, or the whine coming back off far rock walls.

patch.name: Sword clash
patch.description: Two steel blades meet edge to edge in a stone courtyard. 0 ms: the attacker's blade (a long bar, 640 Hz) strikes near its tip. 4 ms later the defender's blade, shorter and held tight so it rings higher and dies sooner, answers. Both are real hand-forged bars, a little out of true. 30 to 260 ms: the edges grind along each other as the swords slide to the guards, a rasp that slows down. A few sparks tick off the contact. Walls give it a short hard slap.

tracks.note: The swung blade: free to ring, struck near the end so every mode sounds. Steel on steel, so the hardest mallet.
The parrying blade: gripped hard (more damping), another object (other variant), 4 ms late. The flam is what makes it two swords.
Edges grinding to the hilt: a scrape exciter on a plate-like blade flat, ridge rate falling as the slide slows.
Flecks of hot steel: a handful of bare clicks right after the hit.

controls.label: Blade size
controls.hint: Daggers, thin and high, to great two-handers.

controls.label: Force
controls.hint: A light tap of blades to a full-strength blow.

controls.label: Ring
controls.hint: Blades caught and deadened, or left singing.

controls.label: Slide
controls.hint: A clean bounce apart, or a long grind down to the guards.

controls.label: Courtyard
controls.hint: Open field, dry, to hard stone walls close by.

patch.name: Sword swing
patch.description: A longsword swung hard past your head, right to left, no contact. The blade is a thin edge moving at 30 m/s half a metre away: 280 ms of air being cut, a narrow whistle that rises as the blade comes and falls as it goes (real Doppler, not a filter sweep), loudest for only 60 ms in the middle. Under the whistle the flat of the blade pushes a duller gust. As it passes, the steel itself sings very faintly, the way a blade hums when it moves fast.

tracks.note: The cutting edge: noise through a tube resonator gives the whistle a pitch, and the doppler bends it past you. The story is in this layer.
The gust off the flat of the blade: lower and softer, a few ms behind the edge. Gives the swing weight.
The steel humming: a long bar excited by a faint scrape of air. Barely there; mute it and the swing becomes a stick.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: A slow heavy arc to a whip-fast cut: shorter and with a bigger pitch bend.

controls.label: Blade
controls.hint: A thin rapier's whistle to a broad greatsword's whump.

controls.label: Whistle
controls.hint: Plain rushing air to a sharp singing edge.

controls.label: Closeness
controls.hint: Across the room to shaving your ear: sharper and more sudden.

controls.label: Steel
controls.hint: A wooden practice sword to ringing steel.
